name: Reduced Launch Cost 4.1
summary: Reduces the cost for launching your ship from the ground. Options for free cost, 5% and 10% of total energy per launch
author: Lex - lo2k
description:
[size=4]Reduced Launch Cost
[/size]
[b]4.1 version is compatible with Cursed 5.29[/b]

Removes or lowers the fuel cost for launching your ship from the ground.
[b]
[/b][b][color=#ff7700]Note 1 : Each ship type uses different fuel quantities when taking-off and playing in survival doubles fuel quantities !
[b]Note 2 : Since a few game updates, you can use supercharged slots to improve fuel efficiency, get ingame technology modules reducing fuel quantity used per launch or even slowly recharging your fuel tank when landed ![/b][/color][/b]

Options for free cost (instead of 25% of energy per launch), 10% and 5% of total energy per launch

[size=3]Installation[/size]
[list]
[*]Unzip the zip file
[*]Pick the desired pak
[list]
[*] 0% cost per launch: ReducedLaunchCost_0.pak
[*]5% cost per launch: Reduced Launch Cost 5.pak
[*]10% cost per launch: Reduced Launch Cost 10.pak
[/list][*]Copy the desired pak file to No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/MODS (Create the folder if it doesn't exist)
[*]Delete No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/PCBANKS/DISABLEMODS.txt if it exists
[/list]

[i]Note:[/i] If the mod doesn't seem to work, you likely have a mod conflict. Try renaming this mod to be last (e.g. XXReducedLaunchCost_0.pak)
[color=#f1c232]This mod is incompatible with any other mod that modifies[/color][b] [color=#f1c232]NMS_REALITY_GCTECHNOLOGYTABLE.MBIN[/color] [/b][color=#f1c232]but a .lua file is provided for each variant if you want to merge it with any other mod written for[/color][b] [/b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957][color=#ffd966]AMUMSS[/color][/url][color=#f1c232]
[/color]

[size=3]Un-installation[/size]
[list]
[*]Delete the selected pak file from No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/PCBANKS/MODS
[/list]

[size=3]Changes[/size]
File: METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/NMS_REALITY_GCTECHNOLOGYTABLE.MBIN

name: Star Trek Binoculars
summary: Binoculars replacement
author: RD
description:
[size=3][size=3][u][b]Description[/b][/u][/size]
This will replace the binoculars with a Star Trek overlay. Three versions, all handmade. Part of my mission to trekify NMS.

[u][b]Features[/b][/u]
[/size][list]
[*][size=3]HD 2048x1024 resolution.[/size]
[*][size=3][size=3]Binocular blue filter removed.[/size][/size]
[*][size=3]Handcrafted vector graphics.[/size]
[*][size=3]Overlay for the survey scanner (keeps the orange filter).[/size]
[/list][size=3]
[size=3][u][b]Files affected
[/b][/u][/size][/size][list]
[*][size=2]Textures\Lut\Filters\BINOCULARS.DDS[/size]
[*][size=2]Textures\UI\HUD\BINOCULARS.DDS[/size]
[*][size=2]Textures\UI\HUD\SURVEYING.DDS[/size]
[/list][size=3]
[size=3][u][b]Installation[/b][/u]
1) Create the folder MODS in \GAMEDATA\PCBANKS of No Man's Sky.
2) Unzip. Copy .pak file to the MODS folder.
3) Rename [b][color=#a4c2f4]DISABLEMODS.TXT[/color][/b] to [b][color=#a4c2f4]zzzDISABLEMODS.TXT[/color][/b].
4) Start the game.[/size]
[/size]
[u][b]History
[/b][/u][size=3]-3.2 Added overlay for the survey scanner. Alternate visor updated for beyond.
-3.1 Fat version brightness outside/inside fixed.[/size]
[size=3]-3.0 Fat and thin updated for Beyond[/size].
-2.0 [size=3]Modified the regular version for the NEXT update. Also replaced the ugly blue filter with a default filter.[/size]
-1.0 [size=3]Added a new one. This is a remake from the binoculars shown in ST TNG 5x17 The Outcast.
Because of the filter the colors are different.[/size]

name: JJs Better Ships
summary: Removes C class from ships and makes S class ships common.
author: JJhookah
description:
JJs Better Ships
[color=#00ff00]Version 5.3[/color]
Author[color=#00ff00] [color=#f4f4f4]JJhookah[/color]
[/color]

                                                                      [color=#00ff00]Updated for Swarm 6.43[/color]
                                                                 See below for Version changes.

Removes C class and makes S Class ships as common as other ships.
All ships types are still available but will be S, A and B class only.
                              
[color=#ffff00]Install[/color]
Step 1 : Extract from zip.
Step 2 : Open the extracted unzipped folder and copy the JJs.Better.Ships folder found inside to your No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder.
Create a Mods folder if you don't already have one.
Ensure mods are enabled in No Mans Sky / binaries / SETTINGS / GCMODSETTINGS.MXML :
<Property name="DisableAllMods" value="false" />

[color=#ffff00]Uninstall[/color]
Delete JJs.Better.Ships folder from No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS

Made with TubOcrisco's excellent NMS MODDING STATION.
[color=#00ff00]
Special Thanks again to Monkeyman192 for updating compilers.[/color]

Would also like to thank JovianStone for help locating a certain file.

Modifies: INVENTORYTABLE.MBIN
                 AISPACESHIPMANAGER.MBIN

Version 1.1 changes

Fixed shuttles, haulers, fighters, explorers and freighters not spawning in S class.

Thanks to Majora4613 for bringing this to my attention.
Also added optional "No Shuttles" version as suggested by Majora4613.
Please only use one version at a time.

Version 1.2 Changes

Added police ship and police freighters. {see new pics}
Made ambient freighter spawns warp in.
Added "warp in" Capital Freighters to secondary "warp in" fleet.
Increased possible size of secondary fleet spawn.

Version 1.2 uses above mentioned files plus: EXPERIENCESPAWNTABLE.MBIN
Uses different files to Redmas "Massive Fleet" but I would not recommend trying to use these two mods together.
Fully compatible with my "Planetary Freighters" mod.
Highly recommend using "No Blinding Freighters" by Lo2k.

Version 1.3 changes

Fixed issue of police ships spawning in place of fighters, especially in Vykeen systems.
[color=#00ff00]
V 1.4 NEXT[/color]

Updated for NEXT
For compatibility and functionality police ships and police freighters have been removed from mod.
Recruitable frigates are only available in ambient spawns  {All spawns that don't have capital freighters}
Recruitable frigates classes are unaffected by mod.

name: Atlas Language Assistant
summary: Come to better understand the infinite through finally becoming fluent in the language of one of its prominent guests.
author: Gmr Leon
description:
[u][b]Notice:[/b][/u] I will be seeking to update this mod for compatibility with Next once we've arrived at a stable version of the game. Until then, the versions currently available are for [i][b]Atlas Rises only[/b][/i]. It may be that they have improved learning the Atlas language with Next, but until I'm certain of that, expect an updated version of this.

Thank you so much for downloading this mod, sharing and enjoying it with others. For those interested in my other mods, I'll be looking to update those that remain relevant once we've arrived at a more stable build of Next that won't necessitate repeated updates to my work and repeated downloads on your end. See you then!

-----------------------------------------------------------

The Atlas Language Assistant aims to improve the rate of learning the language of the Atlas. By making the Atlas' scattered children, the Monoliths, a guaranteed source of at least a few words of the Atlas language. Alongside this, there's another guaranteed source of Atlas language knowledge, but I'll leave you in the dark on where, that you may uncover it for yourself.

Come to better understand the infinite through finally becoming fluent in the language of one of its prominent guests.

[u]Recommended Companion Mod:
[/u]It was brought to my attention that you mightn't be able to learn all the words necessary to understand the Atlas Interfaces, despite my work here, so I told Nyxara (creator of dialogue fixes for Freighter Captains & Nanite/Blueprint Vendors) and they updated their work to address this.

Thus I highly recommend you also download [url=https://nomansskymods.com/mods/nyxaras-dialogue-fix-eng/]Nyxara's Dialogue Fixes!
[/url]
[u]If you liked this, be sure to give my other work a look![/u]
[url=https://rd.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/414]Cockpit Cloak.[/url] Conceal the cockpit so you can record slick videos!
[url=https://rd.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/404]Fireworks![/url] Build a variety of firework launchers to light up the sky!
[url=https://rd.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/570]Project Toaster.[/url] Rework graphics settings to better improve performance on lower end systems!
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/574/]Reforested Lush Planets.[/url] Restore the forests on lush planets incidentally lost with Atlas' Rise!

[u]Tools to Help Understand & Mod the Files[/u]
[url=https://github.com/GmrLeon/NMS-Reward-Allocator]NMS Reward Allocator![/url]﻿ If you've ever wanted to add a reward to every interaction of a certain type, this is the tool for the job! It appends existing or custom rewards to every entry according to your settings in the GUI.
[url=https://github.com/GmrLeon/NMS-Annotation-Script-Generator]NMS Annotation Script Generator![/url] ﻿Generate scripts to annotate the tech, substance, & product tables! Also now updated with a generator to produce scripts to annotate the mission tables!

PStho: if you're diggin' this, come join the moddin' party! We're always down for more folks tweakin' the game and makin' the impossible possible![url=http://nmsmodding.wikia.com/wiki/Getting_Started] Click this to pick up our tricks![/url] Same time, if ya want more active discussion, feel free to check out the [url=https://discord.gg/XzRmehA]NMS Modding Discord.[/url]

name: Joew's No Man's Sky Mod Manager
summary: I made this program to help you easily manage your mods for No Man's Sky. You can enable and disable mods easily and very fast.
author: joewalabel
description:
I made this program to help you easily manage your mods for No Man's Sky

[b]F[/b][u]eature[/u][b]s[/b]:
- Enable and Disable Mods
- Open Mods Folder (for easy extract your mods)
- Check Mods Conflicts (version 2.0+)
- Clean SHADERCACHE folder. (version 2.4+)

[b]R[/b][u]equirement[/u][b]s[/b]:
- . NET FRAMEWORK 4.6.1
- Tested with Steam version, but should work with GOG too.

[b]I[/b][u]nstruction[/u][b]s[/b]:
- Set the Game Folder Path. Steam is: ...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky
- Click Save button to save changes.
- Before Save, make sure NMS game isn't running.
- Click on Refresh button after unzip new mods to your mod's folder while Mod Manager is openned or to undo all changes you made.
- Mouse right click inside mod list area to open mods folder
- To Check Conflicts click on the button at centered bottom and wait the analyzes finish ;)

P.S:
With version 2.0 it now checks mods conflicts.
At the time it only check the conflicts and tell you which files. So you can see all the files are conflicting and can take some action: disables all and enables just one. You can see the mod and file so u can try go to mod's authors and ask them to merge the mods that u want :D or you can do anything else that u want.

Its a bit slower with many mods, sorry. But its because mod manager have to extract all mods and check all files. Not my fault anyway, but on next version ill try optimize it.

name: Better Planet Generation
summary: A huge planet generation overhaul that aims at making your hundreds of hours of exploration in the magnificent, infinite universe of No Man's Sky less repetitive and hopefully even more memorable.
author: WoodyMontana
description:
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][i][b]                                                     [size=6]Better Planet Generation[/size][/b][/i][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738968-1312445652.jpeg[/img]

[size=4][b]More planets

[/b][size=3]Better Planet Generation is a total overhaul of the planetary generation in No Man's Sky.[/size] [size=3]It improves by a significant margin the procedural aspect of the universe while at the same time respecting the original work and vision from Hello Games.[/size]

[size=3]It adds thousands of new distinct environments to the universe[/size][/size]. All of them come in five different life levels and varying placement scales and layouts. These environments were made to seamlessly combine with each other in many different ways.

Better Planet Generation is designed to bring variety to the different biomes you will visit but most of all it brings a lot of variation to the universe. Outside of the countless combinations of assets and their resulting new environments, planets you visit will present themselves differently each time. Placement layouts, scale of the regions, density, variety of assets and their respective scale, ...

No planet will look exactly the same. Unless, of course, it is a very simple one. More on that below.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1631005159-472402214.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-1789086190.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-1298994048.jpeg[/img]


[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=4][b]Sub Biomes[/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Caves and underwater sub biomes have also been entirely overhauled.

Tons of new variants have been added underground and just like on the surface, additional objects can spawn to increase variety even more.

﻿[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410276-924973523.jpeg[/img]﻿

Underwater has been completely revamped and is now generated through a triple layered dynamic framework combining assets to generate highly varied and detailed environments.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738939-165524032.jpeg[/img]
[b][size=4]
Unique planets

[/size][/b][size=4][size=3]On top of all the added variety, BPG also uses a flexible dynamic generation framework that can take many shapes[/size][/size] and create countless planetary variations, even when the same environments are being used multiple times.

Each planet generated has its own selection of parts based on its biome. Some liberties have been taken when designing and attributing those parts to the various biomes. Some objects have been injected to improve variety, but some restrictions have also been applied to preserve each biome's identity. Better Planet Generation also introduces countless restored, modified or repurposed assets to the game in order to increase the variety while preserving its visual style.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936068-132859967.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-754906087.jpeg[/img]

[/size][/size][/size][/size]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Natural Generation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is a vastly different experience compared to the unmodded game and even other biome mods.
Not even taking into account the small details, it is more than likely that you will never be able to encounter all the possible assets combinations this mod can generate. Let alone in the different regional layouts each dynamic template can result in.

Each biome has access to multiple procedural templates. Each producing different results in terms of layouts and objects combinations.
Their common goal is to show you a different kind of environment each time. Aesthetically and structurally.
No more "postcard" planets where most of what there is to see is right around the corner. The scale of the generation can get extremely vast compared to the vanilla game.

Planetary generation can now affect your visual enjoyment and the gameplay.
It is a video game, after all.

A world generated at its fullest possible level and highest complexity can take you some time to fully explore on foot. Meaning seeing the most notable regions (and not all of them) and scanning everything.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630052272-1155900954.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-2086924238.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630272224-118529207.jpeg[/img]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]More Variation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

On the other hand, Better Planet Generation also allows more simple, generic yet still visually interesting planets to see :

- Planets only covered in grass and some plants, rocks or both.
- More barren worlds dominated by giant stone or crystal spires.
- Radioactive wastelands.
- Planets dotted with trees or occasional small forests.
- Volcanic wastelands.
- Toxic fields.
- Rocky swamps.
- ...

And the list goes on and on.
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3]The occurence of these "generic" planets only relies on probabilites. None of my templates is designed to specifically produce them.
I made sure they still looked good, though.[/size][/size][/size][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410296-1590906166.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1626079315-1486130072.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Different Experience[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is not for everyone. Planets can be both very detailed in every aspect or very simple.
If you expect to always see trees and a full grass coverage on your Lush planet or anywhere else, there are other mods for that.
This is not what you should expect using BPG.

Now, whether you are a new player ready to explore an infinite universe or a more weathered one that wants to be surprised by the game again, I suggest you give Better Planet Generation a try. It won't harm your game in any way.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629923717-282604290.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410307-2137550589.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=5]WARNING BEFORE INSTALLING :[/size][/b]

Installing this mod will operate changes to the terrain in every biomes.
It is also recommended to install it while in a space station / anomaly / freighter and not on a planet's surface.
Some major updates to the mod can reset the terrain or biome lists.
I'll include a warning on the download page and the sticky when it's the case.[/size][/size][/size][/size]


Recommended :
[/size][/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/968]DUD's Sky - Colors[/url] : load planetary colour palettes before BPG to avoid procedural textures conflicts.
[/size][/size]

name: Fast Actions 7.1
summary: Faster clicks and key pressed actions
author: Lo2k
description:
Instead of pressing a key for almost one second, this mod provides quicker or instant inputs for :
- menu selection
- creating/dismantling technology
- transfering resources to/from ship
- entering ship
- discussing with NPC
- gathering small plants
- launching refinery processing
- recovering deployable technologies

Enjoy !
[url=http://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/28/?]
[/url]This mod exists in 2 versions :
﻿- instant actions : almost no delay actions (Fractal 4.13 added an in-game option but it only works for a limited range of actions)
- fast actions : between original and instant actions

[color=#ffd966]New : v7.1 fixes precise item quantity amount selection with Instant Actions. (Fast Action is untouched)[/color]

name: HD Space Planet Clouds 2.2
summary: High-Res planet clouds as seen from space
author: Lo2k
description:
This mod is an overhauled atmospheric cloud texture based on Scooterbaga 's [url=https://nomansskymods.com/mods/hd-clouds/][color=#f1c232]HD Clouds mod[/color][/url] 4K texture (8192x4096 pixels).

Scooterbaga's Nasa2 texture was very nice because it's a 4x version of the original game texture but looking at it more closely, I discovered it had a lot of issues here and there, so I did a big pass on it and tried to fix everything I noticed.

In details, this mod fixes the following issues from Scooterbaga's texture (see the last screenshot for a snapshot of my work) :
- removed a sometimes very visible seam appearing verticaly over all the planet at tiling position
- fixed tiling missmatch clouds
- filled holes, low transparency corrections and softened cloud cuts
- removed black dot lines, speckles and scratches
[color=#ffd966]
Note that it only improves long distance clouds as seen from space or from another planet, not the volumetric sky clouds.[/color]

Enjoy.

Optional :
- Add a slow pace rotation movement to your planet atmosphere with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1662][color=#f1c232]Rotating Atmosphere[/color][/url]


[color=#ffd966]history : v2.2 has been updated for 6.21 Remnant game version[/color]

name: Exosolar's and Babs' Beyond Base Building
summary: ★ FULLY MP compatible, this mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options
author: Exosolar Sparky NeptuneX3 Babscoole
description:
[b][color=#f1c232][size=4]What is this Mod?[/size][/color][/b]
[size=4]There are now almost 1,000 buildable base parts in vanilla No Man's Sky! It's a dream come true!
This mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options.
This does NOT mean the mod gives you access to all buildable parts.  You still need to learn the blueprints for each.  :)
Beyond Base Building does NOT add any new build parts to the game.

Now includes all the functionality of gBase Items, [color=#ff0000]if chosen by running the Lua script[/color]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Can multiply power, extraction, and storage rates by 2, 5, or 10. WARNING: Bases built with this mod cannot be uploaded for multiplayer when using 2x, 5x, or 10x multiplied rates.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*][size=4]EM Generators do not need a hotspot and produce 250 power.  Not enabled by default.  Must run Lua through ANUMSS and answer question "Choose a multiplier for Storage and Rates and EMAnywhere status" to generate custom mod file to enable.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]

It is [b]fully compatible[/b] with multiplayer, co-op building, uploading, etc, because it [i]does not add[/i] any parts, which would cause issues in multiplayer.[/size]

[size=4][color=#f1c232][b]★ Beyond Basebuilding[/b] is fully Lua scripted, with script provided for easy updating and merging [b]★[/b][/color] and carries over all of the official updates and improvements offered by Hello Games [b]plus[/b]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Most parts can be Scaled [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] prefab building parts, [color=#fff2cc]Exocraft Geobays, Mineral/Gas Extractors and Base Computer[/color] (Door attachment points bug out when scaled, and issues persist with scaled base computers and geobays).  There may be others not listed.  Be aware, scaling breaks snapping.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built in a Freighter.  [color=#fff2cc][i]Exceptions[/i][/color]  include the Base Computer, Industrial Mining parts, Vehicle Summoners and planet-based teleporter.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built at a Planetary Base [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] the freighter teleporter and the Orbital Exocraft Materialiser[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can be built above and below water[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can change color and material[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts, which can be deleted, can be deleted without also deleting attached objects [color=#fff2cc][i]except[/i][/color] Decals and Posters[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]No build-count limits [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] for parts related to resources harvesting, certain terminals, beacons and message capsules (and others with limits that are hard coded into the game, as they are added or changed by Hello Games).[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Unlimited Storage Containers[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*This does not increase actual storage amounts: Each numbered container acts as an index to the store rather than a physical box[/i][/size][/color][/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Foundation, Pavings and Communications Station can be placed anywhere (not only on bare terrain)[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Non corvette parts buildable with corvettes[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]
Some customization of the mod is available just by running it through AMUMSS, where you'll be prompted about enabling several feature.  Even more customization can be had by editing the top portion of the Lua before processing.  See Lua usage below for link to AMUMSS install and basic usage How to.[/size]

[color=#f1c232][b][u][size=5]Disclaimer:[/size][/u][/b][/color]
[size=3]This MOD makes changes to the placement and usage setting of vanilla parts.  If the MOD is removed, the vanilla settings will be restored and parts that "violate" a vanilla setting as well as those connected may go "poof".  Best practice is to regularly backup your saves for semi-painless recovery from the unexpected.[/size]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

[size=5][b][u][color=#f1c232]Installation[/color]
[/u][/b][/size]
[b]Extract archive contents to GAMEDATA\MODS

[color=#f1c232][size=4][u]Lua usage[/u][/size][/color]
[size=4][b]✦[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626]How to use AMUMSS at No Man's Sky Nexus - Mods and Community (nexusmods.com)[/url]✦[/b][/size][/b]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]Modified Files[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[color=#d8d8d8][size=3]METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\BASEBUILDINGOBJECTSTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color]

[i][color=#cccccc][size=3]Also check out...[/size][/color][/i]
[size=5]✦[b][color=#ffdd00][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/58018181?tab=user+files]Exosolar's Other Mods[/url][/color][/b]✦[/size]


[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

[size=5][u][b][color=#f1c232]Is this Mod up-to-date?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4][i][b]Any mod files which are not hidden or demoted to the "Old Files" area can be expected to work.[/b][/i]
All uploaded files (on the Files page) are maintained with their packing date and version of the MBINCompiler used to pack it. Older mod versions, no longer compatible with the current version of No Man's Sky will be demoted to the "Old Files" subsection, but will remain available for download. There are no side-effects to using this mod.[/size]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]How to update, tweak, combine, or patch the mod with AMUMSS?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4]As this mod is now Lua scripted, you can [color=#fff2cc]easily [b]update[/b], [b]tweak[/b] or [b]merge[/b] the mod yourself[/color] (if a game update breaks this PAK of the mod, or you have other PAK or Lua mods that could conflict with this one). [color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*Click on the spoiler below for more[/i][/size][/color][/size]
[spoiler]
[size=3][u]Notes on AMUMSS:[/u]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] tries to update [url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler/releases]MBINcompiler[/url] automatically. If it fails to convert EXML/MBIN files, its likely due to a very recent NMS version update and MBINcompiler is awaiting an update too.
If so, I highly recommend you to disable your mods and wait for MBINCompiler to be updated (it's pretty quick in general).[/size]


[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Updating the mod after a game update:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][list]
[*] [size=3]Download [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url], and extract it locally,  avoid placing the AMUMSS folder in a path with special characters or in a system folder like [color=#fff2cc][i]"C:\Program Files (x86)\(...)"[/i][/color].[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Place the mod Lua script (only the .LUA file, not the .PAK file) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]AMUMSS will normally auto-detect the NMS installation folder, but you can also manually edit the path in the [color=#fff2cc][i]NMS_FOLDER.txt[/i][/color] file.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root of the AMUMSS folder and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]A new modded PAK file will be created, using the last update of the MBIN game files duly amended by the script.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]Most of the time simply recompiling the mod using the Lua script will make it compatible again. Use the latest script to ensure you adopt any mod adjustments to accommodate the latest NMS build.[/size][size=3] There are two main causes of mods not correctly updating with this method:
1) MBINCompiler needs an update to be able to decompile the latest version of the game MBIN files.
2) Structural changes have been made to the MBIN files called by this Lua script. Whilst unlikely, this will require some script rewrite and other mods are likely affected.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Tweaking the mod:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]Use the same process as described in [color=#fff2cc][i]Updating the mod[/i][/color].
Just modify the script as you want before recompiling it. Look at the top of my scripts, you can generally edit modifiers there, or even disable/enable some features very easily.[/size]

[size=3][color=#cccccc][i]*[url=https://notepad-plus-plus.org/]Notepad++[/url] or [url=https://code.visualstudio.com/download/]VSCode[/url] are generally recommended to read EXML and Lua files, due to large file support and automatic highlighting. The [url=https://sourceforge.net/projects/npp-compare/]Compare plugin[/url] for Notepad++, and Lua is also a must-have to highlight file differences.[/i][/color][/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Combining mods that provide Lua scripts:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You'll want to do this if multiple mods affect the same MBIN file.[/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Place all the scripts in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Follow the step, selecting that you want to combine all the scripts into one PAK file, and the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]AMUMSS will output a PAK file that will contain the modifications of all the scripts.[/size]
[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]*If the scripts modify the exact same values in the MBIN file, the last loaded script will overwrite the preceding script values.[/i][/size][/color][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Patch in the mod to make it compatible with other PAK files:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You will want to do this if another mods isn't Lua scripted, and affects the same MBIN file as the Lua scripted mod.

It will work when :
Case 1) you patch a Lua scripted mod for only one other PAK.
Case 2) you patch a Lua scripted mod for several other PAKs, but only if the other PAKs don't modify the same MBIN files between them.[/size]

[size=3][b]How to create a patched PAK:[/b][/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Copy the script and the other mod(s) PAK(s) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS, and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]The new PAK file will contain all the Lua script modifications, and a compatibility patch for the other mod(s) PAK(s).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Rename it something like [color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz Scripted Mod Name -Patched For- The Other Mod Name.pak"[/i][/color].[/size]
[size=3][color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz"[/i][/color] prefix is to ensure that it'll be loaded after the mod(s) it was patched for (for NMS loading order, underscore [i]"_"[/i] came after every other characters).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Remove the original scripted mod PAK from the [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder, and copy both the new patched one, and the other mod(s) PAK(s), into it.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=3][u]Notes:[/u]
[b]Be sure the mod PAK you want to create a compatibility patch for, is updated for the latest NMS version.[/b]
-> When AMUSS find an MBIN file affected by a script and by a PAK in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder, it will take the MBIN file from the mod PAK over the original one of the game, and will apply to it the modifications listed in the script.
So, if the MBIN file of the mod PAK is not updated, the one in the resulting patched PAK won't be either.[/size][/spoiler]
[/spoiler]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]
[color=#f1c232][u][b][size=5]Philosophy[/size][/b][/u][/color]
[size=4]All the erroneous limitations in building are pretty silly, aren't they? In making this mod, I paid specific attention to making sure I did not make changes that will invalidate the bases built with it from online play. Any base made with Beyond BaseBuilding will be fully viable and visible in online play, even when other players don't have this mod! It does this by only editing placement rules while you are in the building editor and not modifying any of the actual base parts themselves.
We hope you enjoy the mod and naturally, your comments are most welcome. We can also be found on the No Man's Sky Discord or reached directly at: [color=#f1c232]Babscoole #6326 [/color]or [color=#f1c232]Exosolar#5120[/color], or if its about the Lua script: [color=#f1c232]NeptuneX3#8095[/color] [size=3][i][size=4]or [/size][/i][/size][color=#f1c232]s p a r k y#0536[/color][/size]

And, of course, thanks to all of the other modders who make mods too, as we often inspect the work of other modders to learn how things are done: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/12249518]RangerDulann[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/1964784]WoodyMontana[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/42286415]jasondude[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/38106355?tab=user+files]Gumsk[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/45932167?tab=user+files]Mjjstral[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/41291360]moddinaccount[/url], Devilin Pixy, saa044, and others have all helped us learn to mod effectively! files.changelog_html: NMS 6.40 Swarm update

3.73: Updated to 3.73.  Some minor changes to the LUA for compatibility with AMUMSS 3.9.5.X+ syntax checking
3.81: Updated to 3.81.  Using a non-public nightly release of MBINCompiler, so fingers crossed.  :)
3.82: Update to 3.82.  Hopefully fixed the color issue, as all platforms are using the same game file version.
3.97: Update for 3.97.  First swing at Endurance compatibility.  Lots of stuff left to go over, so a work in progress
3.98: Update for 3.98.  Planter boxes now available on freighters.  Removed build limits to datasign.
3.99: Lots of Endurance "fixes".  GeoBays buildable on Freighters again (Change GEOBAYS_ON_FREIGHTER to true in LUA and run through AMUMSS, false by default).  Added back many other items by default as well.  Farm plants plantable in any biome.
4.03: Change to the LUA script only for use with AMUMSS 4.0.0.5.  Will be prompted in AMUMSS if you want GeoBays on freighters.  No changes to the mod itself
4.06: Update for 4.06.  Added Base storage containers to freighters, off by default.
4.08: Added FREIGHTERROOMS_ON_PLANETBASE.  By default disabled.  To enable, run the lua script through AMUMSS.  Say yes to enable global input.  When prompted, say Y to enable "Freighter Tech and Bio rooms on Planet Bases".  Overwrite old .pak with the new one generated.
4.38: Changes to the Lua ONLY.  Made some changes to prevent warnings/notices in AMUMSS when combining/merging with certain other base building mods.  Renamed the script to change AMUMSS processing order when combining/merging with certain other base building mods that could lead to a game crash.
4.45a: Removed planet build limits for Firepit and Spawner Ball
4.62: Update for Orbital.  Incorporates some changes from gBase Items
4.65a: MARINESHELTER_ABOVE_WATER now true by default.  Combined EMAnywhere and Multiplier selection into one prompt in the Lua
4.65b: Fixed typos in the multiplier prompt in the Lua script.  Geobays should now be scalable by default.  Fixed some notices when certain optional features were enabled via prompt when Lua is run.
4.72: Add Base Salvage Capsules on Freighters, add optional NPCSTATION_ON_FREIGHTER
5.26: Update for NMS 5.26.  Increase number of landing pads per planet base by 25%
5.28: Update for NMS 5.28.  Increase power range in freighters
5.28a: 2nd attempt at increasing free power range.  1st broke airlock door working, so reverting and trying from Bridge Connector.
5.29: Add anomaly seal (S16_HEATER) to freighter build
6.00: Compatibility for NMS 6.00 update.  Thee have been no changes dealing with corvette parts.  I'll look into that in coming days.
6.01: Hopefully added all parts not available in corvettes to corvettes.  I fully expect this to need to be dialed back a bit.
6.03: Fixes issue with double Short Range Teleporters
6.04: Update for NMS 6.04.  Added AMUMSS prompt to place Corvette parts on Planet Bases to script, so don't need to manually edit the script.  Default is Y
6.06a: Correct old typos in Lua script
6.23: Fixed a labelling error in the Lua script
6.33: Resolved issue with freighter tech rooms not showing up for some people in corvettes
6.34: Remove base build limit for wonder projector.

name: Increased Draw Distance and LOD
summary: This mod increases planetary terrain LOD and draw distance and flora and LOD and draw distance.
author: Battou
description:
Beyound update drasticly decreased already low model detail distance and draw distance. This mod tries to fix that. Terrain loda and detail draw distance increased about 5 times, also planet sooner switches to detailed terrain as you aproach it. Flora and rocks, crystals etc LOD distance increased adout 3 times, draw distance increased as far as I could, it seems to be somehow bind to terrain patche loading.

CAN BE VERY PERFORMANCE HEAVY!! Have not tested it on Low and Mid range PCs.


There is now 8 versions of the mod!

-Normal, with increased draw distance and LOD distance, but with standart grass draw distance.
-With increased grass draw distance.
-With no Fade in/out shader effect.
-With increased grass draw distance and no Fade in/out shader effect.

And LIGHT versions of ll four main versions thar have draw and LOD distances decreased x1/3 times compared to main mod versions. Must be more performance friendly.

Also added:
-Full version with increased grass draw distance, merged with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1102]True clouds and Slow clouds[/url] by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/87374]Lo2k[/url] and applyed grass slope growth fix from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1080]Grass fix 4[/url] mod by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/58018181]Exosolar[/url] (but not the whole mod).

-Light version with increased grass draw distance, no fade-in/out shader effect, merged with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1102]True clouds and Slow clouds[/url]﻿ by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/87374]Lo2k[/url]﻿ and applyed grass slope growth fix from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1080]Grass fix 4[/url]﻿ mod by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/58018181]Exosolar[/url]﻿ (but not the whole mod).

name: Freighter Base Floor Plan
summary: This is more of a tool than a mod; a floorplan mapping spreadsheet I've devised to assist with the planning and design of Freighter Bases.
author: Snuggs McAllister
description:
Unlike base building on a planet, It is hard to see what you are doing when building a Freighter Base in No Man's Sky. You are completely enclosed and cannot see any further than what you have already built. You have a large grid to work with, you can build upwards 14 levels and you have a much more limited number of pieces with which to build than you do planet-side.

   I drew some preliminary schematics in pencil for how I wanted to build my base levels, but it didn't take much erasing to decide that I needed to build my map on a computer program. I searched the web and found that I was in completely virgin territory - I was going to have to build it myself. I decided to build a mapping tool on a spreadsheet program. I'm very pleased with my results and decided to share my little toy with the community.

   What I've made is artistically detailed, but very simple. I've set up a spreadsheet with a 22 x 21 grid of squares representing each Freighter Base level. Above this are clickable and draggable 'pieces' representing the Freighter Base building parts in the game. 

   By copying and pasting these parts onto the grid you can, piece by piece, build a map of your future or existing Freighter Base. Right-clicking reveals options to help you orient each piece and simply cutting without pasting will remove pieces that you wish to remove.
   And voila - I've turned a spreadsheet program into a computer mapping tool. You can toggle into and out of game to consult your spreadsheet diagram as you build if you have just one monitor, but those with multi-monitor set-ups will have their Freighter Base Map right next to them as they build! You can also roll 'old-school' if you prefer by printing a copy and base building with your 'blueprint' right next to you.  The spreadsheets are print-ready - all you have to do is fill in the grid with your base plans.

   What this 'Mod' provides:

[list]
[*]Tabbed spreadsheets in OpenDocument (.ods) format, which can be downloaded from the internet for FREE from LibreOffice and OpenOffice. The floor tabs are bottom left.
[*]22 x 21 grid representations of each floor of you Freighter Base. (The Endurance update expanded this from a 21 x 21 grid)
[*]Movable base building 'pieces' representing every configuration of in-game Freighter Base design. These pieces are proportionally 'accurate' to one another and snap into place next to each other like puzzle pieces. Once you have filled each grid you will have an accurately mapped representation of each level of your base.
[*]A versatile way to 'play around' with building choices before you commit in-game resources.
[*]A method to ensure maximum utilization of space.
[*]A precision instrument for constructing accurately proportional representations of Freighter game-space.
[*]The option to print a level-by-level map of each floor of you Freighter Base.
[*]A way to share with one another the basic designs of Freighter Bases. I would LOVE to see your designs, so feel free to post images!
[/list]
   This 'Mod' does NOT provide:

[list]
[*]Creativity. I've attached an image of my own base to show you what I've done, but beyond that you'll need to come up with your own ideas about how you would like your Freighter Base to be.
[*]Changes of any kind to the game world. This is not a mod - just a tool to be used Outside of game. You must still utilize in-game resources to build you base in No Man's Sky. Freighter Base Floor Plan provides no in-game short-cuts or cheats.
[*]An automatic base building generator. You have to design each level of your base yourself, piece by piece, just like in the game.
[/list]
   You will need LibreOffice or OpenOffice to use this mod as intended. Although I originally designed this on Excel not everyone has that program installed on their computer and I no longer have access to a copy myself presently. LibreOffice and OpenOffice are free downloads and I've redesigned my spreadsheet to work perfectly with them. Those that open this file with Excel will find that it works, but you will have to re-scale the pieces to properly fit the grid, or re-scale the grid to fit the pieces.

   I have also written a new READ ME included with the download, which contains some directions and a short FAQ to help everyone out because, to be frank, my 1.2 Update introduced some added complexity. You will be Stacking pieces on top of each other far more than before.

   I've posted my own floor plan to provide an example of what can be done with Freighter Base Floor Plan and I'd love to see what you create, so feel free to post pictures of your own layouts to help provide creative inspiration for the rest of us!



   I appreciate your interest in my modest efforts and hope they prove useful to someone!


     - Snuggs

name: Better Rewards
summary: Increase the amount of currency you get with faster word learning and increased resource gathering options. Frigate (Freighter) Expeditions are also included!
author: MrTrack
description:
Better Rewards increases the amount of units, nanite clusters and quicksilver you get from completing missions or interacting with objects in the world. Non npc word learning (such as knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also faster.

[color=#bf9000][size=3]IMPORTANT NOTE: Don't use this mod when I haven't updated it to the new game version (especially when it is a new or returning expedition)
[/size][/color][color=#bf9000]if you really want to use it when I haven't updated it yet, make sure you [/color][color=#bf9000]back up your save[/color][color=#bf9000] or build the mod using the lua scripts yourself.[/color]

[b]Currency[/b]

Currency gain is roughly increased by 5 times, so as to make it a viable option besides crafting and selling valuable trading goods. Some unit values were tremendously increased (eg.: from minimum amount of 1000-2000 to 20000-50000) like the terminals in abandoned settlements to make the early game less grindy.

Includes:
[list]
[*]Space station missions and Nexus missions
[*]Interactable objects/devices (abandoned buildings, damaged machinery, waypoints, etc.)
[*]Sentinels
[*]Alien interactions
[/list]
[b]Words[/b]

Learning words from non npc interactions (knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also 3 times faster (3 words learned form a single knowledge stone). You now also learn 5 Atlas words, instead of 1 and also have a chance (15%) to learn them when interacting with non npc learning sources.

[b]Resources

[/b]When gathering with the mining beam you generally get 2 times more resources (but only when the things explode as you mine them). Also includes containers, depots, guild rewards, asteroids and ships that drop resources.

[b]Frigate (Freighter) Expedition Rewards

[/b]After a successful expedition, when collecting your rewards you get 5x more units and nanites, 2x more products like Storage Augmentation and NipNip Buds and 3x more resources like Copper, Emeril and Cadmium.
[b]
Installation

[/b]Make sure you delete or edit DISABLEMODS.TXT in your game library (...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS) before trying to use mods. Extract the zip file to ...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder and you are good to go (Create MODS folder if you don't have one). Alternatively you can just use Vortex to download and install.

This mod modifies the [color=#ff0000][size=3]REWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] and [color=#ff0000][size=3]EXPEDITIONREWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] file and will not work with other mods that use those tables.

[b]Updated to NMS version 6.21 (Build ID: 21918502) on 2026.02.13.[/b]

name: Merging tutorial
summary: A quick tutorial to explain how to merge mods
author: Methatronc
description:
Hello,

You want to use different mods but they are overwriting each other ?
You are at the right place ! We will start with the basics, hang on it is quite easy you will see :)

[u][i]A Few Basics[/i][/u]

First of all you need to understand that a mod is a .pak file that mainly contains .mbin and .dds files.
The .mbin files are used for configuration, and the .dds are for the textures.
When there is a conflict when using multiple mods, it means that the file(s) that is modified by a mod is also modified by another mod.
That is why some mods are released like this : "___mymod", because order is important, and therefore something is likely not going to work. Hence the importance of merge.

When having an issue, two things are to be checked :
﻿_is the mod up to date? => if yes, go to the next step, otherwise try contacting the author.
﻿_is the file(s) modified by the mod modified by another mod? => if yes you will have to merge if you want to keep them both.

Before going on with it, remember to backup the mods you intend to modify, if you mess up at some point you won't have to download your mods all over again if you have a backup :)

[i][u]External Softs
[/u][/i]
Now for the merge, you will need only three software and a plugin :
﻿[url=https://github.com/periander/PSArcTool]_PSArcTool [/url]to extract the .pak
﻿[url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler]_MBINCompiler [/url]to extract the .mbin ( take the latest version )
[url=https://notepad-plus-plus.org/downloads/] ﻿_Notepad++[/url] to do the merge ( take the latest version, 64 or 32 bits depending on your computer, [url=https://i.imgur.com/diKTJ9W.png]here to check[/url] )
﻿[url=https://github.com/pnedev/compare-plugin/releases/tag/v2.0.0_npp7.7]_Compare[/url] to simplify the merge ( again, take the latest version, [url=https://github.com/pnedev/compare-plugin/releases/download/v2.0.0_npp7.7/ComparePlugin_v2.0.0_npp7.7_X64.zip]64[/url] or [url=https://github.com/pnedev/compare-plugin/releases/download/v2.0.0_npp7.7/ComparePlugin_v2.0.0_npp7.7_x86.zip]32[/url] bits depending on your computer, [url=https://i.imgur.com/diKTJ9W.png]here to check[/url] )

PSArcTool and MBINCompiler are not installers, so you just have to [url=https://www.7-zip.org/]unzip[/url] them in a folder, eg "NMSEdit".
Install Notepad++, once it is installed unzip the Compare archive you have downloaded and place what is inside in a folder named ComparePlugin, that you will place in "C:\Program Files\Notepad++\plugins" or in "C:\Program Files (x86)\Notepad++\plugins" for the 32 bits version.

You are done with installation ! Congrats, now let's merge the mods :)

[i][u]The Merge[/u][/i]

You have to identify the problematic file, ie the one that is used by two or more mods, just look at the page description of your mods for that : when the author says " it should work as long as no other mod modifies xxx.mbin ", note that file somewhere if you have too much mods to remember what files they modify, and do it for each mod you use, that is the only way to be sure that you won't overwrite something when installing a new mod. Then if you notice a file that is edited by two mods you have it !

Take the conflicting mods to your "NMSEdit" folder, place each one in a different subfolder, say "mod A" and "mod B". Open two windows, one in NMSEdit and one in mod A. Drop the .pak on PSArcTool.exe, it will process the mod and extract the content. Now drop the .mbin on MBINCompiler.exe, it will convert it into an editable .exml file. Do the same for the mod B.

You now should have two .exml files named alike, say ﻿﻿GCUIGLOBALS.GLOBAL.EXML for both.
Open these files with notepad++ ( right click/open with ) and on the first file click on the 1 button on the picture below, and on the 2 for the second file :

[img]https://i.imgur.com/MDXlNmr.png[/img]

It will generate two windows like above, where you can see the differences between the two files you have. For instance, here mod A is changing space units to conventional units and mod B is hiding the number of damages made in combat. What mod B is changing is indicated by 3, the line in the Compare NavBar which says there is a difference above in the files. What you want is to combine the two mods : you will make the changes to one of the file,( usually I pick the one that has the fewer changes to be made ), so that the merged file has its own modification but also the one that are added by the other mod.

Here, we would go higher where 3 indicates a change, and modify a value from true to false, which is the point of mod B. Only one change from mod A to B, three from B to A. In this example it does not sound like a big deal but some .exml can have hundreds or more of modifications compared to another mod, so always go with the easiest way :) 

Now you just have to save the changes, delete the old .mbin, drop your modified .exml on MBINCompiler.exe, pack you merged mod with PSArcTool.exe and you are good to go ! In our example, we modified mod A so that it does the same as mod B plus what mod A does. But mod B was only composed of one file : the one we took the modifications from. If your mod is composed of more files than just the conflicting ones, you still have to put mod B in your folder MODS, but remember to remove the files that you have taken the changes from,( ie delete them and use PSArcTool to pack a new mod B that does not contain the conflicting files).

That's it ! I hope that was clear enough, if not don't hesitate to ask in comment.

Thanks a lot for the continuous efforts of monkeyman192 for MBINCompiler, for periander's useful soft, to the notepad++ team, to pnedev for his notepad plugin and of course to Hello Games for NMS and the assets used in the picture !

Have fun :)

Methatronc

name: NomNom
summary: NomNom is the most complete savegame editor for NMS but also shows you additional information around the data you're about to change. You can also easily look up each item individually to examine its attributes, independently of a savegame, or get other useful information that are not related to a specific one (but enhanced if one is loaded).
author: zencq
description:
[color=#e69138][size=3][b]NomNom is now in beta state.[/b] This means for you that some things may still not be 100% finished but the general state of the tool is a lot better than before.[/size] If you encounter bugs or when you think something doesn't work as expected or could be improved, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1566?tab=bugs]let me know[/url]![/color]

[color=#ff0000]All available features are tested while implemented but mistakes can happen, so be aware of that and backup your saves![/color]

The features can be divided into the different main parts:
[list]
[*][b]Manager[/b] Manage your saves!
[list]
[*]Automatic backup.[/*]
[*]Save your save as human-readable JSON.[/*]
[*]Copy, move, and swap slots to another.[/*]
[*]Delete your save.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][b]Editor[/b] Edit your save for your needs!
[list]
[*]Ability to manage fleets, change data values like currencies and stats, and organize inventories.[/*]
[*]Ability to fast travel to any system you like, trigger space battles, and clear portal interference.[/*]
[*]Ability to edit your knowledge and recorded experiences.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list]
Have a look at the screenshots as well, to see what NomNom is capable of.

Each version of NomNom is built with the latest game version (at that time) in mind and the version number is reflecting that. Each one is also backwards
compatible down to [b]Beyond 2.11[/b] and even saves before that can still be edited via the build-in JSON editor. If you use it with a newer game version branch than
the one it was built for (e.g. [b]7.00[/b]), things should work as usual in most cases but there can always be a breaking change.

NomNom is compatible with every platform No Man's Sky is available on (some work better than others though). You can select a specific account/folder with you saves or, for platforms on PC, one level above if you have multiple accounts. A complete and always up-to-date overview with additional notes can be found [url=https://github.com/zencq/libNOM.io?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started]on GitHub[/url].


[b]Instructions[/b]
[list=1]
[*]After downloading and extracting the zip file you'll find a few files. All you need to care about is the executable ([b]NomNom.exe[/b]) but new folders may    be created at runtime (e.g. for backups) that will become relevant to you.[/*]
[*]You may want to create a shortcut to the executable for easier access.[/*]
[*]As the tool includes an automatic backup functionality you don't need to do it manually but if you want to be absolutely safe, do it.[/*]
[*]At first start the tool locates your saves at the default location of each platform but if that fails, you must select it manually.[/*]
[*]Select a slot.[/*]
[*]Start tinkering![/*]
[/list]

If you like NomNom and want to support me in its further development, you can do so via the donation options above or on [url=https://www.buymeacoffee.com/cengelha]Buy Me a Coffee[/url], [url=https://github.com/sponsors/cengelha]GitHub[/url], [url=https://ko-fi.com/cengelha]Ko-fi[/url], and [url=https://www.patreon.com/cengelha]Patreon[/url]. I will appreciate it!
There won't be a paywall though.

The is also a dedicated [url=https://discord.gg/nomnom-762409407488720918]Discord[/url] server where you'll find all information in one place, firsthand. Please read the rules first, to gain full access. If you need (or want to offer) help, found a bug, have a suggestion, or something else regarding NomNom, you will find, or can post it there.

Issues created here on Nexus Mods or via another channel will of course also be addressed.


Header image by [url=https://patreon.com/Orioto]Orioto[/url]﻿.

name: Normalize Economy Names (AMUMSS)
summary: Removes unnecessary names from economy level, economy class and conflict levels. Does not alter gameplay just UI strings.
author: thmsn
description:
This is a script that uses [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] to do what the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/657?tab=description]Normalize Economy Names[/url] mod did.

Removes unnecessary names from economy level, economy class and conflict levels. Does not alter gameplay just UI strings.

I have generated .pak files for PRISM 3.53 and added them as files
[list]
[*]The main vortex file is English
[*]Other languages are in optional files
[/list]
If there is an update in the future you can use the AMUMSS scripts to generate a new .pak file accordingly
[size=3][b]## Instructions[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Download & Extract [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url]
[*]Place the desired `NEN_[LANGUAGE]_everything_AMUMSS.lua` file into the `ModScript` folder of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url]﻿
[*]Run `BUILDMOD.bat` from the extracted [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url]﻿﻿ folder
[*]When asked
[*][quote]??? Would you like to COPY the created Mod PAKS to your game folder and DELETE [DISABLEMODS.TXT] [Y,N]?[/quote]
[*]Press [b]Y[/b]
[*]When asked if you want to check for mod conflicts, Press [b]N[/b]
[*]Wait for ~5 minutes while the script is generating the mod
[*]The generated mod should now be present in your Mods folder and you can launch NMS
[/list]
[b]## Other notes[/b]
[list]
[*]`[b]REPORT.txt[/b]` will contain the result of running `[b]BUILDMOD.bat[/b]` if you are interested in seeing what the .lua file changed
[*]`[b]LANGUAGE/NMS_UPDATE3_[LANGUAGE].MBIN[/b]` is being modified.
[*]You can run `[b]BUILDMOD.bat[/b]` with an empty `[b]ModScript[/b]` folder and press `[b]Y[/b]` when asked for checking conflicts to see if there are any conflicts between your currently installed mods.
[/list]

name: No Man's - Prepare to Sky Edition (PTSd) -- A Progression-Difficulty-Balance Overhaul
summary: A balance overhaul to achieve 5 things: improve difficulty (mostly optional now), balance rewards away from passive options towards a variety of active playstyles, make the choice between weapons/starships/multi-tools more distinct and meaningful, slow down progression to stretch out the early-mid game, and a few bug fixes and new features.
author: Xen0nex
description:
[center][size=6]No Man's - [b]P[/b]repare [b]T[/b]o [b]S[/b]ky E[b]d[/b][/size][size=6]ition[/size]
(PTSd)[/center]
[size=2]The title is [i]mostly [/i]a joke: while by default PTSd does attempt to substantially increase the challenge of combat, exploration, trading, farming, etc. while reducing many "overpowered" income options, you can reduce most of that back down with the in-game Difficulty Settings. Even with the default settings, a number of activities / rewards / costs are actually improved from vanilla, such as Settlement rewards, the loot from most exploration activities, Class upgrade/Pet unlock prices, larger Refiner stacksizes, etc. And much of the mod is not centered around difficulty at all, but instead on improving balance or adding new options.[/size]

[center][size=5][b]Goals of this mod[/b][/size][/center]

If you enjoy [b]starting new save files[/b], the [b]sense of progression [/b]of a [b]new character[/b] through the [b]early & middle portions of the game[/b], and start to lose interest once your character has [b]unlocked everything[/b] and can do anything easily, and prefer [b]choices[/b] without[b] overpowered or underwhelming options[/b], PTSd may interest you. Covering many aspects of the game through a wide range of [b]cost/value/reward adjustments, rebalanced equipment stats, improved enemy combat stats, [/b]and[b] a few added features[/b], PTSd aims to:

[list]
[*]Remove or restrict most "[b]overpowered[/b]" get-rich quick schemes, such as market crashing, chlorine refining, Activated Indium mines, scrapping Interceptor ships, etc.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Stretch out the early & mid-game[/b] so the player is not able to immediately buy any & everything. Generally there will be more time where the player can be "looking forward" to unlocking various tech or features that are currently unavailable or unaffordable.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Make buying & [b]using weaker C Class ships or upgrade modules[/b] early on more appealing, as the higher class items should be expensive enough to prevent the player from simply always just buying the highest quality options available.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Make it [b]more rewarding[/b] when the player eventually is able to get higher class starships / multi-tools or better exocraft, or invest upgrades into them, especially since enemies / the environment are challenging enough to appreciate the added ease / convenience they bring. Generally there will be a more noticeable gap between the performance of a fresh Class C piece of equipment, and a maxed out Class S full of upgrades.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Increase the base [b]challenge [/b]of most [b]combat encounters[/b] (can largely be offset with various combat-related in-game Difficulty Settings)[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]As much as possible, avoid situations where either [b]one playstyle is so clearly superior[/b] to the alternatives that they aren't worth considering, or the inverse where an [b]option is completely underwhelming[/b] compared to others. For example, in Vanilla an Activated Indium mine or Fusion Ignitor farm are orders of magnitude more profitable than any other activity, while conversely Settlements, salvaging Crashed Freighters, or rescuing Freighters from pirates typically provide so little reward that it is hard to justify the time taken to do them. In PTSd the rewards of many activities are more comparable, although they each still have advantages or disadvantages.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Relatedly, in general reduce the gap between "[b]passive[/b]" forms of income such as [b]Extractors/Farms/Frigate Expeditions[/b] and "[b]active[/b]" income such as [b]exploring, finding & selling valuables, destroying spaceships, completing space station missions[/b], etc. so that "passive" income doesn't completely overshadow "active" income, and "active" play is encouraged more.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Similarly, differentiate & balance the Multi-Tool / Starship [b]weapons [/b]and [b]Multi-Tools[/b] / [b]Starships [/b]themselves so that there is no "[b]clear winner[/b]" which is statistically superior to all the others. E.G. Why pick the Neutron Cannon when the Scatter Blaster kills everything much quicker? Or why pick a Hauler when you can upgrade an Exotic to just as much storage with excellent stats? Or why pick a Royal/Experimental/Pistol when an Alien Multi-Tool has higher Damage (which also improves mining speed), and the Scan stats provide negligible benefits? In PTSd the various kinds of equipment and weapons are both made more distinct from each other with more noticeable differences in speed, abilities, etc. while still making sure each has a specialty or niche that makes it worthwhile. For example, the [b]Mining [/b]and [b]Scan [/b]stats for [b]Multi-Tools[/b] now directly improve the resources / units you receive when mining/scanning things.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Add more ways of [b]steadily earning Nanites[/b] throughout the game.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Add more ways of obtaining [b]Tritium,[/b] [b]Di-Hydrogen[/b] & [b]Salvaged Data[/b] to the mid/late game.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Correct some [b]Vanilla bugs[/b] such as the Ship Agility stat only affect maneuverability while boosting, or supercharged slots making the mining laser/scanner tech slower instead of faster, or mining speed being affected by both the Mining and Damage stat bonuses on your Multi-Tool, or certain items / effects having typos in their values making them far stronger/weaker than intended, etc.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]When possible, clarify unintuitive vanilla mechanics or PTSd changes that are particularly important with [b]expanded descriptions[/b] on techs/items/buildings/Difficulty Settings (see bottom of the [b]Customization [/b]section below on how to make these PTSd changes to vanilla in-game text display on computers set to languages other than [b]English[/b]).[/*]
[/list][list]

[b][size=3]General Difficulty Changes[/size][/b]

[*]Because PTSd raises the base challenge of various aspects of the game, the individual effects of various [b]difficulty settings[/b] have been tweaked so that "[b]standard/normal[/b]" options for most difficulty options reflects the [b]base PTSd experience[/b], more or less equivalent to playing the previous version of PTSd on Survival mode pre-4.0. Additionally, due to the increased difficulty of Frigate Expeditions, you will likely be completing fewer Expeditions per day initially, further slowing down the growth of fresh Frigates. [*]Note that as in vanilla, the listed DPS for weapons / multi-tools shown in the inventory menu is [b]not very reliable[/b], e.g. a starship weapon with a lower displayed DPS may actually do far most "real" DPS than one with a higher displayed DPS.[/*]
[*]Because core weapon techs typically gain a huge, but unequal boost when supercharged (Usually a +40%~60% improvement to DPS for a maxed out weapon), all core weapon techs have had their attributes divided by the same factor that supercharging multiplies them (this includes the attributes which are better to be low, such as reload time, recoil, or inaccuracy, since supercharging oddly makes those worse by increasing them). Thus [b]most weapon techs start out underpowered[/b], but [b]supercharging them[/b] brings them back up exactly to their "default" strength. In essence, this means PTSd is balanced around the assumption that you are [b]always using core weapon techs on a supercharged slot[/b] as a matter of course, since they gain so much benefit from them.[/*]
[*]  ﻿  ﻿﻿This is applied to all weapons on multi-tools, starship weapons, exocraft. Also partially applied to all kinds of mining lasers, but only to the damage & heat rate, not the damage tickrate or resource yields[/*]
[*]  ﻿  ﻿Note: As in Vanilla, while most weapons benefit most from supercharging the core tech, Cyclotron Ballista & Blaze Javelin (charged shots) get more benefit from supercharging an upgrade module instead (Neutron Cannon was "fixed" in PTSd to always benefit from supercharging the core tech by making the charge time improve from supercharging). (Blaze Javelin rapid shots benefit more from supercharging the core tech)[/*]
[*]  ﻿  ﻿On the flipside, Photon Cannon and Positron Ejector gain huge benefits from supercharging, having only around half their "default" DPS when "fresh" if not supercharged, though slightly less of a gap when "maxed out".[/*]
[*]As in Vanilla, most "maxed out" weapons will also have their DPS increase by 1.2x~1.3x when supercharging an upgrade module(if it contains a multiplicative bonus like fire rate), compounding for each upgrade module that is supercharged (Depending on slot placement: often losing adjacency bonuses to move an upgrade module onto a supercharged slot may cancel out some/most of the benefit from supercharging it).[/*]
[*]However also like in Vanilla, a few weapons gain very little DPS benefit from supercharging either the core tech or upgrade modules once maxed out(only +~10% for core tech, and much less for upgrades/secondary tech). These are the [b]laser [/b]or [b]explosive [/b]based weapons: [b]Phase Beam/Gazing Eyes, Rockets, Plasma Launcher, Geology Cannon, [/b]and[b] Blaze Javelin[/b]. These may be appealing as "secondary" weapons or in situations where you don't have extra supercharged slots to spare, since you can still get very close to their peak DPS (once maxed out) without having to use a supercharged slot(s) on them.[/*]
[*]  ﻿  ﻿Blaze Javelin is a special case that actually gets worse DPS when firing charged shots when the core tech is supercharged due to it increasing weapon charge time.[/*]
[*]  ﻿  ﻿Blaze Javelin also gains very little rapid-fire damage from supercharging the core tech, and also gets little benefit from supercharging upgrade modules either. Because of this, its core tech values were not lowered to compensate for supercharging, since it is rarely worth supercharging at all.[/*]

[*]  ﻿  ﻿﻿﻿Starship [b]maximum upgradeable inventories have been reduced;[/b] instead of the typical vanilla max of 110/60 for Cargo/Tech, the new baseline is [b]30/40[/b], although most specific ship types are adjusted as listed below. [center][size=5][b]Usage[/b][/size][/center]

PTSd alters many relevant [b]in-game item/tech/difficulty setting descriptions and dialogue options[/b] so that generally anything critically important can be found simply by paying attention to [b]in-game text[/b] (in English, for other languages see the [b]Customization [/b]section below). By default PTSd is mainly balanced around using the "[b]Survival[/b]" preset and[color=#ffffff][font=Roboto, sans-serif] not using the the starship target assist, although of course you can choose/change any of the in-game Difficulty Settings or Controls to make things easier/harder as you like[/font][/color]. Also, some of the [b]Recommended Mods[/b] below work very well alongside PTSd.

Generally PTSd aims to address different playstyles / strategies directly, however there were a few things I was unable to change (although again, many of these should have in-game reminders in the relevant UI descriptions / dialogue window):
[spoiler]

[*]While PTSd has the biggest impact when starting a new save file, it also works on existing saves. If continuing an [u]existing non-PTSd save[/u], several things such as which recipes are unlocked from the start, various inventory sizes, the stats of your existing starships / freighter / multitools will retain their old values. Upgrading its Class (A to S, etc.) will cause it to use updated stats, or you can use a [url=https://github.com/goatfungus/NMSSaveEditor]Save Editor[/url]﻿ to manually change the inventory sizes & stats to match PTSd values, or to forget certain recipes such as Freighter Trade, Refiner, or Cultivation Rooms, or Freighter Storage Rooms higher than Room #0. Also be aware of possibly losing some resources from full stacks if changing to a smaller stack size.[/*]
[*]It should be safe to disable PTSd and continue playing the savefile in Vanilla, or even to temporarily disable PTSd and re-enable it later on. However if you play the same save file while it is uninstalled you may need to re-install any of the few PTSd-added techs afterwards and may now know some recipes which PTSd leaves unknown by default. Just be aware of how high you have your valuable resources stacked if moving to a lower stack size, or the stats/slots of any starships/freighters/multitools you acquire or upgrade the Class of with PTSd uninstalled.[/*]
