files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.03
files.changelog_html:
Fixed issue with weapon grip animations: all Multi-Tools should now use their proper vanilla grip animations, so Rifles etc. should be held in two hands like normal again.
• On average, new Multi-Tools should have ~0.7x as many initial slots on them, between 6~16 depending on their size category(maximum upgradeable size is unchanged at 24 slots). There is also no longer any "overlap" in slot amounts between size categories, i.e. all "Medium" (Like Royals) will always be found with more slots than any "Small" Multi-Tools (like Pistols) and fewer slots than any "Large" Multi-Tools (like Rifles)
• A hidden benefit for smaller sized Multi-Tools is that their supercharged slots are more likely to be grouped towards the left half of their inventories compared to larger Multi-Tools. This both makes it more likely to unlock and discover the supercharged slots sooner while upgrading them, but also a little more likely that supercharged slots might be adjacent to one another as there are fewer possible slots for them to appear in. (This same behavior also exists in vanilla, but has been amplified in PTSd)
The Exocraft / Minotaur Cannon's critical hit multiplier is now just 1.1x instead of 1.5x, as its large AOE makes it very easy to strike critical weak points no matter where it actually hits enemies.
The refiner recipes to convert Residual Goop --> Viscous Fluids --> Living Slime --> Runaway Mould now each complete 5x faster, and Runaway Mould --> Nanites completes 1.5x faster. This should make it less prohibitively time-consuming to make use of all the Goops & Slimes found while exploring.
Also buffed the Atlantideum + Mordite --> Living Slime recipe, as on top of taking an extraordinarily long time, it was vastly less efficient at converting Atlantideum into Runaway Mould than simply using some of the Atlantideum to create Pugneum and make Runaway Mould directly. It now completes 120x faster, and is ~20x more efficient, but makes Residual Goop instead of Living Slime. This makes it a bit more efficient, but require more time & steps than the alternative (Atlantideum + Pugneum --> Runaway Mould)
Removed the 1.2x bonus to Settlement products output rate, as it seems the game may not actually round down the products per cycle as the UI implies it does after all. Also lowered the "stocked" item cap for Settlement output from 9999 items to 3600 items, which should still hold ~3 days worth of Substance production for a highly-developed Settlement, and still holds ~120 days worth of Product production (although anything past a week or two is already straining the "normal gameplay" situation)
Added clarification to the in-game descriptions of the various Difficulty presets on how they fit with PTSd
Added clarification to the in-game description for the Ground Combat Difficulty Setting that the "Hostile" option also increases the chances for some planets to have Aggressive Sentinels, particularly Lush planets (this is a vanilla effect, it just normally isn't explained to the player)
A tiny bit more .lua cleaning: AMUMSS should no longer should give a Conflict warning about "MOD_BATCHNAME.LUA" (which could be safely ignored)

files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-503-0-5-1723066200.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.03
files.changelog_html:
(This change was accidentally not implemented in PTSd v503.0.3) Significantly increased the crafting cost of the Liquidator Mech parts. They now all require several Recycled Circuitry and potentially other trade / farm crafting products, at least 1 million units worth of materials each.
Corrected an oversight in vanilla NMS for how it handles Mining Speed bonuses based on Multi-Tool's type stat bonuses. Now a Multi-Tool's "Damage" stat bonus no longer also increases mining speed, so Multi-Tool types with high "Damage" bonuses but low "Mining" bonuses should be noticeably slower at mining, as intended.
Vile Queen health increased a further ~1.33x
Rebalanced the possible items found in all kinds of Suspicious Packets:
• (Tech) Packets now can also have Pulse Engine & Launcher X-Class upgrades, and both (Tech) and (Arms) Packets can have various upgrades for Exocraft / Minotaur / Nautilon. Since those upgrades don't come in X-Class, they will randomly be C/B/A/S Class, with lower chances for higher Classes.
• (Goods) packets have the chances to award Repair Kits or Walker Brains reduced 0.5x, various Trade Goods reduced ~0.15x, and the possible amounts for many items such as Trade Goods, Geodes, Larval Cores, Gravitino Balls, etc. increased 2~4x
The unsalvageable "mini-shipwrecks" added in NMS 5.0 are now roughly half as likely to yield Suspicious Packets (Tech) instead of Suspicious Packets (Goods) or Anomaly Detectors
Removed Conflict Scanner and all starship/multi-tool weapon techs except for Pulse Spitter, Plasma Launcher, and Phase Beam from the random tech reward pools. In exchange, added more low-level "utility" techs to the random tech reward pools such as Simple Translator, Shield Lattice, Personal Refiner, Emergency Warp Unit, Instability Engine, etc. In PTSd these random tech rewards mostly come up in the "Expanding the Base" missions, and default to a related upgrade module instead if you've already learned all the techs.
Similarly, the Armourer NPC now awards Efficient Thruster & Ablative Armour techs alongside a tech from the random ship tech pool instead of the Cyclotron Ballista and Infra-knife Accelerator techs.
Emergency Warp Unit blueprints now also sold by shops in Minor Settlements, not just at the Anomaly
Hex Core value increased ~1000x (was worth 16 units previously)
Slight adjustments to possible loot for killing anomalous creatures on Weird / Exotic / Anomalous planets, they now drop less Mordite / Hex Cores
Increased number of Gravitino Balls required for some "Expanding the Base" missions from 10 to 24

files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-503-0-6-1723325764.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.03
files.changelog_html:
Updated the Multi-Tool comparison chart on the Description page to give a better idea of each Multi-Tool's actual mining performance. Split the previous "Mining" stat bonus for each Multi-Tool type into showing both the resulting "Resources/object" (how much substances you get per mined rock/tree/crystal/metal finger/etc.) and "Resources/sec" (how quickly you can receive substances while mining, taking into account both how quickly you mine rocks/trees and how much substances each will contain).
Increased the "Resources/object" amount on the unique Mining Laser variants Hijacked Laser by 1.6x and Runic Lens by ~1.16x, to make the Sentinel & Atlantid Multi-Tools more competitive with Pistols for mining:
• Now Sentinel Multi-Tools can reach the highest "Resources/sec" in theory, however in practice this may be a bit lower due to the increased time you will need to take to keep aiming at new rocks/trees with how quickly they get destroyed, plus needing to walk to new areas after destroying all nearby rocks/trees, plus needing to pause more frequently to cool down the laser as it heats up more quickly. And this is on top of consuming fuel at ~6x the rate of other mining lasers.
• Now Atlantid Multi-Tools are closer to Pistols for "Resources/sec" (though still below them & Sentinel Multi-Tools), however in practice it may be a bit higher as they will take less time aiming at new rocks/trees with how slowly they get destroyed, slower heating up, etc. (essentially the opposite of all the points above for Sentinel Multi-Tools, aside from having default fuel consumption)
Scanning stat bonus increased ~1.07x for Atlantid & Staff Multi-Tools
Damage stat bonus increased ~1.1x for Alien Multi-Tools
Starship Rockets were working a little too well early on, so their overheat cooldown is increased 1.5x and base damage decreased to ~0.85x, so you will have to be a little more choosy when to fire them. However, the damage bonus from the Large Rocket Tubes tech is increased to now be +100% instead of +50% of the base damage, so the final maxed damage is slightly higher than before. Also clarified in the in-game description that the Large Rocket Tubes tech improves damage, not cooldown (not improving cooldown appears to be a vanilla bug).
Further increased how much having an active shield protects against Technology Damage/Breaking: tech breakage is now ~0.67x as likely as before while your shield still remains. As usual, breakage chance still increases the lower your shields get like in vanilla (and no change to tech breakage chances with shields down). Can be adjusted in "PTSd Other Difficulty Settings.lua".
Adjusted some space station / nexus mission reward chances: higher chances for low-level missions to award Defence Chits, much lower chances for high-level Nexus missions to just award trade goods / storm crystals, replaced Hexite reward with more valuable Hex Cores, a few other tweaks
Adjusted some prices for items bought from Scrap Dealers (w/ Tainted Metal) / Outlaw Stations (w/ Units):
• Repair Kit: Tainted Metal price decreased 0.8x, Units cost increased 2x
• Suspicious Packets (Tech): Tainted Metal & Units price increased 1.25x, (Arms) Packet: Tainted Metal & Units price decreased 0.8x (their prices should now be closer together)
Possibly fixed an edge case where in some situations, sending a frigate fleet with a rating 2 stars above the frigate expedition difficulty rating may still have had a chance to take damage. As a side effect, 4 star difficulty expeditions are now rarer and 3 star difficulty ones are more common.
If re-paking the default PTSd .luas, down to 5 Warnings & 4 Notices

files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-505-0-1-1724106266.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.05
files.changelog_html:
Hopefully addressed (at least partially) the issue of Pirate Raiders one-shotting the player at certain buildings / POI locations:
• Planetary Pirate Raids have been disabled from spawning at Planetary Colossal Archives in "PTSd Longer Space Wanted Level Countdowns.lua" (due to a vanilla bug where they directly target the player when spawning at that location). If you notice the bugged "directly targeting & one-shotting the player" Pirate Raid behaviour elsewhere, please let me know what the nearest building / POI was so I can potentially disable that as well.
• Pirate Raiders now spawn ~4x farther away from the player, which should now give enough warning time to get indoors / underground just in case there are any other locations which are also bugged. They also now spawn in groups of up to 8 starships instead of up to 12.
• As a failsafe, added a new toggle to completely disable planetary pirate raids at the top of "PTSd Other Difficulty Settings.lua"
Decreased the substance mining rate for C/B/A Class Mineral/Gas hotspots by ~0.14x-0.29x (S Class unchanged). Previously, despite differences in mining rates, any class hotspot could easily fill up all attached Silos overnight, which is a common use case. While 8 extractors over either an A & S Class hotspot can still fill a full set of 16 Silos in a day (and on A Class can even fill a half-set of 8 silos overnight, for bases splitting silos between 2 or more substances such as for gas & mineral), only S Class will mine fast enough to accumulate significant amounts during a typical play session. B Class needs just over 2 days to fill a full set of silos, or can get a half-set ~77% full after a day. C Class needs ~3 days to fill a full set of silos, or can get a half-set ~55% full after a day.
Overhaul to increase Pirate Dreadnought battle difficulty & rewards, overview below:
• The battle is more of a true "race against time" / "DPS check" now, with the role of the Anti-Freighter Cannons & Pirate Frigates essentially swapped from vanilla. In PTSd it is no longer feasible to destroy the Cannons fast enough to extend the battle, so the civilian freighter will essentially be taking constant slow damage the whole time. However, you can now destroy most of the Pirate Frigates (the Dreadnought will continually summon replacements once it is down to 2 Frigates) at the start of the battle so that you waste less time taking out the Torpedos, which still need to be continually shot down to prevent the Dreadnought from warping away too soon.
• In order of increasing difficulty (& rewards), the ways to succeed at a Dreadnought battle are now:
• • A) Deal enough damage (via destroying Exposed Fuel Rods) to cause the Dreadnought to warp away, while the civilian freighter survives, for a "small" bounty.
• • B) Fully destroy the Dreadnought (can deal some extra hull damage before destroying the final few Exposed Fuel Rods to prevent it from warping), while the civilian freighter survives, for a "medium" bounty.
• • C) Force the Dreadnought to surrender (by destroying the Warp Drives before all the Exposed Fuel Rods) while letting the civilian freighter die, then demanding a "large" tribute from the Dreadnought.
• • D) Force the Dreadnought to surrender as in C, but do it fast enough that the civilian freighter survives, then collect both the "medium" bounty and demand a "large" tribute from the Dreadnought (this is difficult to pull off & likely only possible with a fairly late-game setup)
• Each of the above success methods requires approximately ~1.5x as much damage output / DPS as the previous method, and the units/nanites reward is roughly ~1.5x as valuable (with more rare items such as Salvaged Frigate Modules / Cargo Bulkheads, etc.). However even if you fail, you should at least now get a few consolation items from destroying some Pirate Frigates & most of the destructible parts on the Dreadnought
• Claiming a Pirate Dreadnought now costs 350,000,000 units instead of being free (still potentially a good deal if the Dreadnought has high slots and Class). However due to modding limitations I haven't found a way around yet, this cost is currently paid each time you inspect the Dreadnought, not when actually confirming the exchange. Added notes about this to the dialogue window to tell the player to use their Analysis Visor instead to inspect the Dreadnought and decide whether to purchase it (and summon their freighter to uninstall any technology first) before making the purchase.
Dreadnought battle change specific details:
• Added a few additional Pirate starship spawns to the battle for a little added hazard, however they essentially remain stationary in a cluster where they spawn and act as a sort of turret/obstacle to avoid due to some sort of vanilla pathing issue.
• Health for Dreadnought hull increased 4x, Shield Generators/Exposed Fuel Rods/Anti-Ship Turrets increased ~8x-22x, Anti-Freighter Cannons increased ~35x, and Warp Drives increased ~52x
• Pirate Frigate health reduced 0.5x, but battle starts with 8 instead of 6 initial Pirate Frigates
• Destroying Exposed Fuel Rods now deal 1.12x as much Dreadnought hull damage. Dreadnought attempt to warp away at 16% remaining health instead of 25% remaining health (this breakpoint can still be achieved by destroying all 10 Exposed Fuel Rods)
• Dreadnought only summons reinforcement Pirate Frigates when down to 1 remaining Frigate instead of 5. Will now only summon 1 Frigate at a time instead of 3
• Dreadnought Anti-Freighter Cannon damage to civilian freighter reduced to ~0.89x, Pirate Frigate Torpedo damage reduced to ~0.77x
• Shield Generators now have a chance to drop Starshield Batteries, Warp Drives & Exposed Fuel Rods have a chance to drop Frigate Fuel (50t), Anti-Ship/Freighter Turrets/Cannons drop ~16/~100 Nanites, and Pirate Frigates drop the same loot as "Easy" PTSd Pirate starships.
• Fixed UI countdown for Dreadnought warp to display accurate time remaining, which doesn't actually get increased by destroying Warp Drive likes the vanilla UI shows (apparently a vanilla bug) Added some other notes/hints to some of the UI for Dreadnought battles to make some things clearer
• Reduced units reward for saving civilian freighter back to vanilla amounts, however added several hundred nanite & a Salvaged Frigate Module or Cargo Bulkhead reward alongside them. Demanding tribute from surrendered Dreadnought units reward increased 1.75x, added ~1,300 nanites, Salvaged Frigate module, & Cargo Bulkhead alongside it
Player-controlled Dreadnought Anti-Freighter Cannons no longer one-shot unshielded Sentinel Freighters / other Dreadnoughts
Slightly increased Phase Beam & Cyclotron Ballista damage vs. Freighter Hulls, slightly decreased Infra-Knife Accelerator damage vs. Freighter Hulls
Increased Shield health for neutral freighters by ~2x (not Sentinel freighter, Pirate Dreadnought, or lead civilian freighter attacked by Pirate Dreadnought)
Decreased base starship weapon damage vs. Planetary Sentinels & Walking Buildings ~0.1x (explosion AOE from starship weapons still deals significant damage)
Decrease the shield-leech effect of Phase Beam & Grafted Eyes to 0.8x. Added notes to in-game descriptions explaining that the relative shield leech effect is greater the higher the user's max shield capacity is. E.G. A Hauler gains much more shields per second using a Phase Beam than a Fighter does, since it has larger shields and they get restored on a & basis.
Increased Hijacked Laser resource yield by ~1.44x to account for how supercharging it divides its yield by 1.2 instead of multiplying it by 1.2 like all other mining laser variants do, and using an un-supercharged mining laser will always be inferior for mining. The Multi-Tool comparison chart left as-is since it already shows the correct proportional comparisons once they're all supercharged.
Freighter Scanner Room requires an Atlas Seed of 1 tier lower, but now costs 3 Navigation Data to scan each star system (in-game description updated to reflect this)
Reduced the % chance for Cargo Scan Deflector / Neural Shielding to succeed on each attempt from 50% to 30%. However since you can make multiple attempts during each scan, using it 2-3 times will still have an overall ~51%-66% chance to work by the end.
Increased units bounty for the weakest version of the "wild" wandering pirate bounties by 1.5x
Destroying the components surrounding Salvageable Scrap cores yields Rusted Metal instead of Ferrite Dust and yields ~0.25x as much
Replaced two of the Gek-specific settlement item outputs with ones worth ~2x more (and can still be cooked / crafted into even more valuable forms): Pie Case changed to Cake Batter, Magno-Gold changed to Enriched Carbon.
Applied the relevant PTSd price modifiers to various uncooked "batters" themselves like Cake Batter, Thick, Sweet Batter, etc.
Added in-game notes to relevant dialogue windows regarding the main "honour-system"/"recommended" PTSd actions such as refusing free rescued freighters, stopping Exosuit slot upgrades at 40 tech & 40 cargo, defeating nearby Sentinel Mechs before shutting down Sentinel Pillars, etc.
Added more clarifications to the in-game Difficulty Setting descriptions to list the actual numerical effects of the various options (based on the PTSd modifiers), or to clarify some unintuitive side effects for some of the settings
Added clarification to in-game description for Cargo Scan Deflector / Neural Shielding that it also works for Pirate Scans as well (like in vanilla).
Added some more PTSd-specific details to in-game descriptions for the Analysis Visor and various types of Mining Lasers to explain how the yield is affect by Multi-Tool stats, note not to combine different types of Mining Lasers, and for Boltcaster/Photon Cannon/Positron Ejector to note any unintuitive features.
Added note to description and Installation.txt about using search tools like grepWin to more easily find things in the PTSd .lua files.

• Planetary Pirate Raids have been disabled from spawning at Planetary Colossal Archives in "PTSd Longer Space Wanted Level Countdowns.lua" (due to a vanilla bug where they directly target the player when spawning at that location). If you notice the bugged "directly targeting & one-shotting the player" Pirate Raid behaviour elsewhere, please let me know what the nearest building / POI was so I can potentially disable that as well.
• Pirate Raiders now spawn ~4x farther away from the player, which should now give enough warning time to get indoors / underground just in case there are any other locations which are also bugged. They also now spawn in groups of up to 8 starships instead of up to 12.
• As a failsafe, added a new toggle to completely disable planetary pirate raids at the top of "PTSd Other Difficulty Settings.lua"
Decreased the substance mining rate for C/B/A Class Mineral/Gas hotspots by ~0.14x-0.29x (S Class unchanged). Previously, despite differences in mining rates, any class hotspot could easily fill up all attached Silos overnight, which is a common use case. While 8 extractors over either an A & S Class hotspot can still fill a full set of 16 Silos in a day (and on A Class can even fill a half-set of 8 silos overnight, for bases splitting silos between 2 or more substances such as for gas & mineral), only S Class will mine fast enough to accumulate significant amounts during a typical play session. B Class needs just over 2 days to fill a full set of silos, or can get a half-set ~77% full after a day. C Class needs ~3 days to fill a full set of silos, or can get a half-set ~55% full after a day.
Overhaul to increase Pirate Dreadnought battle difficulty & rewards, overview below:
• The battle is more of a true "race against time" / "DPS check" now, with the role of the Anti-Freighter Cannons & Pirate Frigates essentially swapped from vanilla. In PTSd it is no longer feasible to destroy the Cannons fast enough to extend the battle, so the civilian freighter will essentially be taking constant slow damage the whole time. However, you can now destroy most of the Pirate Frigates (the Dreadnought will continually summon replacements once it is down to 2 Frigates) at the start of the battle so that you waste less time taking out the Torpedos, which still need to be continually shot down to prevent the Dreadnought from warping away too soon.
• In order of increasing difficulty (& rewards), the ways to succeed at a Dreadnought battle are now:
• • A) Deal enough damage (via destroying Exposed Fuel Rods) to cause the Dreadnought to warp away, while the civilian freighter survives, for a "small" bounty.
• • B) Fully destroy the Dreadnought (can deal some extra hull damage before destroying the final few Exposed Fuel Rods to prevent it from warping), while the civilian freighter survives, for a "medium" bounty.
• • C) Force the Dreadnought to surrender (by destroying the Warp Drives before all the Exposed Fuel Rods) while letting the civilian freighter die, then demanding a "large" tribute from the Dreadnought.
• • D) Force the Dreadnought to surrender as in C, but do it fast enough that the civilian freighter survives, then collect both the "medium" bounty and demand a "large" tribute from the Dreadnought (this is difficult to pull off & likely only possible with a fairly late-game setup)
• Each of the above success methods requires approximately ~1.5x as much damage output / DPS as the previous method, and the units/nanites reward is roughly ~1.5x as valuable (with more rare items such as Salvaged Frigate Modules / Cargo Bulkheads, etc.). However even if you fail, you should at least now get a few consolation items from destroying some Pirate Frigates & most of the destructible parts on the Dreadnought
• Claiming a Pirate Dreadnought now costs 350,000,000 units instead of being free (still potentially a good deal if the Dreadnought has high slots and Class). However due to modding limitations I haven't found a way around yet, this cost is currently paid each time you inspect the Dreadnought, not when actually confirming the exchange. Added notes about this to the dialogue window to tell the player to use their Analysis Visor instead to inspect the Dreadnought and decide whether to purchase it (and summon their freighter to uninstall any technology first) before making the purchase.
Dreadnought battle change specific details:
• Added a few additional Pirate starship spawns to the battle for a little added hazard, however they essentially remain stationary in a cluster where they spawn and act as a sort of turret/obstacle to avoid due to some sort of vanilla pathing issue.
• Health for Dreadnought hull increased 4x, Shield Generators/Exposed Fuel Rods/Anti-Ship Turrets increased ~8x-22x, Anti-Freighter Cannons increased ~35x, and Warp Drives increased ~52x
• Pirate Frigate health reduced 0.5x, but battle starts with 8 instead of 6 initial Pirate Frigates
• Destroying Exposed Fuel Rods now deal 1.12x as much Dreadnought hull damage. Dreadnought attempt to warp away at 16% remaining health instead of 25% remaining health (this breakpoint can still be achieved by destroying all 10 Exposed Fuel Rods)
• Dreadnought only summons reinforcement Pirate Frigates when down to 1 remaining Frigate instead of 5. Will now only summon 1 Frigate at a time instead of 3
• Dreadnought Anti-Freighter Cannon damage to civilian freighter reduced to ~0.89x, Pirate Frigate Torpedo damage reduced to ~0.77x
• Shield Generators now have a chance to drop Starshield Batteries, Warp Drives & Exposed Fuel Rods have a chance to drop Frigate Fuel (50t), Anti-Ship/Freighter Turrets/Cannons drop ~16/~100 Nanites, and Pirate Frigates drop the same loot as "Easy" PTSd Pirate starships.
• Fixed UI countdown for Dreadnought warp to display accurate time remaining, which doesn't actually get increased by destroying Warp Drive likes the vanilla UI shows (apparently a vanilla bug) Added some other notes/hints to some of the UI for Dreadnought battles to make some things clearer
• Reduced units reward for saving civilian freighter back to vanilla amounts, however added several hundred nanite & a Salvaged Frigate Module or Cargo Bulkhead reward alongside them. Demanding tribute from surrendered Dreadnought units reward increased 1.75x, added ~1,300 nanites, Salvaged Frigate module, & Cargo Bulkhead alongside it
Player-controlled Dreadnought Anti-Freighter Cannons no longer one-shot unshielded Sentinel Freighters / other Dreadnoughts
Slightly increased Phase Beam & Cyclotron Ballista damage vs. Freighter Hulls, slightly decreased Infra-Knife Accelerator damage vs. Freighter Hulls
Increased Shield health for neutral freighters by ~2x (not Sentinel freighter, Pirate Dreadnought, or lead civilian freighter attacked by Pirate Dreadnought)
Decreased base starship weapon damage vs. Planetary Sentinels & Walking Buildings ~0.1x (explosion AOE from starship weapons still deals significant damage)
Decrease the shield-leech effect of Phase Beam & Grafted Eyes to 0.8x. Added notes to in-game descriptions explaining that the relative shield leech effect is greater the higher the user's max shield capacity is. E.G. A Hauler gains much more shields per second using a Phase Beam than a Fighter does, since it has larger shields and they get restored on a & basis.
Increased Hijacked Laser resource yield by ~1.44x to account for how supercharging it divides its yield by 1.2 instead of multiplying it by 1.2 like all other mining laser variants do, and using an un-supercharged mining laser will always be inferior for mining. The Multi-Tool comparison chart left as-is since it already shows the correct proportional comparisons once they're all supercharged.
Freighter Scanner Room requires an Atlas Seed of 1 tier lower, but now costs 3 Navigation Data to scan each star system (in-game description updated to reflect this)
Reduced the % chance for Cargo Scan Deflector / Neural Shielding to succeed on each attempt from 50% to 30%. However since you can make multiple attempts during each scan, using it 2-3 times will still have an overall ~51%-66% chance to work by the end.
Increased units bounty for the weakest version of the "wild" wandering pirate bounties by 1.5x
Destroying the components surrounding Salvageable Scrap cores yields Rusted Metal instead of Ferrite Dust and yields ~0.25x as much
Replaced two of the Gek-specific settlement item outputs with ones worth ~2x more (and can still be cooked / crafted into even more valuable forms): Pie Case changed to Cake Batter, Magno-Gold changed to Enriched Carbon.
Applied the relevant PTSd price modifiers to various uncooked "batters" themselves like Cake Batter, Thick, Sweet Batter, etc.
Added in-game notes to relevant dialogue windows regarding the main "honour-system"/"recommended" PTSd actions such as refusing free rescued freighters, stopping Exosuit slot upgrades at 40 tech & 40 cargo, defeating nearby Sentinel Mechs before shutting down Sentinel Pillars, etc.
Added more clarifications to the in-game Difficulty Setting descriptions to list the actual numerical effects of the various options (based on the PTSd modifiers), or to clarify some unintuitive side effects for some of the settings
Added clarification to in-game description for Cargo Scan Deflector / Neural Shielding that it also works for Pirate Scans as well (like in vanilla).
Added some more PTSd-specific details to in-game descriptions for the Analysis Visor and various types of Mining Lasers to explain how the yield is affect by Multi-Tool stats, note not to combine different types of Mining Lasers, and for Boltcaster/Photon Cannon/Positron Ejector to note any unintuitive features.
Added note to description and Installation.txt about using search tools like grepWin to more easily find things in the PTSd .lua files.

Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.05
files.changelog_html:
Further increased the amount of hits the AI-piloted Minotaur must take before getting damaged by ~1.17x
Corrected Phase Beam / Grafted Eye shield leech effect accidentally getting reduced 0.75x instead of 0.8x in previous update
Corrected Ares initially using the wrong item name when asking to trade for Gold Nuggets / Glowing Minerals
Corrected Shuttle & Explorer Shield Bonus at Class C accidentally being ~0.72x as high as intended
Fixed the vanilla quirk where some starships could sometimes can have a Stat Bonus be lower at a higher Class than a lower Class, by making small adjustments to certain Stat Bonuses at certain Classes for Fighters, Haulers, Solars, Interceptors, and Freighters. Now higher Class starships should always have higher Stat Bonuses than lower Class starship of the same type.
Updated some weather event values: Meteor Storms should last 1.5x longer, greater chance of tornadoes being in clusters, some other small tweaks to match things to newer vanilla values
Added Runaway Mould to the list of items which can be refined together with Microprocessors to create Salvaged Data
Added notes to in-game descriptions of all items which can be refined directly into nanites or Salvaged Data (with Microprocessors), and Basalt into Silicate Powder
Added notes to in-game descriptions for Gravitino Balls/Albumen Pearls/Sac Venom and their plantable versions on how they can be refined together to make Di-Hydrogen / Tritium and their relative strengths as "profit" crops
Added hint to in-game descriptions for various "Junk" items like Living Slime or Rusted Metal on how they can be refined into more useful items
Added notes to in-game mission log & popups for handing in Derelict Freighter Crew Manifest / Captain Logs to clarify the different rewards for turning in to different NPCs in PTSd

files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.05
files.changelog_html:
Changed Shield Generators in Dreadnought / Sentinel Freighter battles to use the same damage multipliers as starship shields, so anti-shield weapons will work better against them. (added "Shielded" note to their UI name popup in the yellow shield font color to indicate this)
Changed the damage multipliers vs. non "boss" Freighter Hulls (all except Dreadnought or Sentinel Freighter) for Phase Beam, Cyclotron Ballista, and Infraknife Accelerator back to the same as vs. regular ship Hulls. Positron Ejector still has reduced damage vs. all freighter hulls since it is easy to stay in optimal range against them, but it's damage vs all freighter hulls is now increased ~1.16x to be more competitive with Infraknife Accelerator
Increased the health for some variants of Cargo Pods attached to freighters by 2x to match the other variants.
All kinds of Cargo Pods no longer display their contents before destroying them, the UI now says "Contents Unknown". Will cost more time & standing loss to gather specific items from raiding freighters now.
Reduced rewards from Cargo Pods attached to/nearby freighters in Outlaw systems due to their relatively light defenses: amounts of substances and illegal trade goods reduced ~0.3x-0.5x, relative chance for getting the higher-value illegal trade goods reduced ~0.5x
The value markup for selling illegal goods in non-Outlaw systems reduced from +200% to +100%. However, the base value of illegal goods (including Nip Nip Buds) increased 1.5x so the final selling value outside Outlaw systems remains the same. The main difference is that now there is a smaller profit margin when buying illegal goods in an Outlaw Station to resell in non-Outlaw stations

files.changelog_html:
Exo-Skiff now requires Cadmium and larger amounts of Salt, Crystal Sulphide to build
Automated Trap now requires Emeril, Living Pearls, and larger amounts of Metal Plating to build
Increased the crafting costs for all Fishing Baits, especially for higher grade baits. They all now require increasingly large amounts of either raw or cooked fish, so that you cannot sustainably use the highest quality bait forever without sometimes using lower quality/no bait to replenish your "bait fish" supply.
Adjusted bonus values on Rusted upgrade modules from fishing to fit PTSd patterns
Did some rough units value balancing on foods cookable with any fish, or ones requiring additional non-fish ingredients (Will need to do more in-depth balancing on cooked fish in general)
Corrected vanilla issue where Rusted Launcher upgrade modules from fishing had higher Boost Speed bonuses than C Class Launcher upgrade modules
Added clarification to settlement expedition prompts that in PTSd they generally increase settlement population on average

files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.11
files.changelog_html:
Corrected vanilla issue of Optical Drill being removed from multi-tool tech unlock tree in the Anomaly
Reduced average waiting time between fish bites/catches to approximately ~0.75x, and reduced the window where you can catch a fish after it bites from ~2 seconds to ~1 second.
Improved the bonuses to fish quality for all kinds of bait (including using food as bait), especially Spicy Chum and Bionic Lure. Specialized Baits (Mealworms, Bionic Lure, Dangling Orb, etc.) now also give small improvements to fish size chances, not just fish quality.
Slight adjustments to fish size chance based on sea depth for smoother transition of Medium size fish appearing and less Small fish in deep waters
Bionic Lures now require Circuit Boards instead of Living Glass to craft
Greatly increased units value of raw fish (~10x vanilla value) to be more competitive with other activities for earning units such as collecting Storm Crystals, Ancient Bones, etc. Raw fish no longer have increased sale value on space stations.
Value of foods cooked with fish are balanced around always using the cheapest fish possible. Generally this means only Common (C Class) fish are worthwhile to cook in most cases (Exceptions are Starfish are worth cooking at B Class, and Squid & Turtles are worth cooking at A Class), and recipes requiring "any fish" are balanced around using Common, Small fish.
Slightly reduced nanite value for releasing fish (~0.9x vanilla value), added clarification to UI that releasing fish yields nanites
Automated Traps now take ~2 hours per catch instead of ~1 hour, and can only hold 0.5x as many Common / Uncommon fish per stack
Fixed Automated Traps accidentally being buildable unlimited times per planet in last PTSd patch. Automated Traps can now be built 9x per planet, but still only 3x per base or nearby cluster.
Medium & Large Refiners can now be built 4x each in a nearby cluster (still unlimited amount per base, as long as you put a little spacing between clusters)
Increased nanite unlock price for Fishing Rig tech 2x

Further reduced time needed to reel in a fish after it bites to ~0.5x-0.67x the time in the previous update
Reduced Common (C) & Uncommon (B) raw fish units value to 0.5x & ~0.8x, increased Rare (A) & Legendary (S) raw fish units value ~1.1x & 1.5x. All Colossal fish now only worth 400% of Small fish units value instead of 500%.
Reduced nanites value for releasing Common & Uncommon fish to ~0.3x & ~0.5x, increased nanites value of Rare fish by 1.1x and Legendary fish by ~2.3x to better match their high units sale value
Mealworms rarity bonuses slightly reduced so that it catches noticeably more Common fish than Uncommon fish
With the above changes, now the pattern is that Mealworms / Spicy Chum / Bionic Lure each increase your average units or nanites profits while fishing by roughly ~1.4x / ~2.1x / ~2x compared to the next lowest tier of bait (or no bait in the case of Mealworms) when considering the units cost of bait. E.G. using Bionic Lure gives roughly double the units or nanites profits compared to Spicy Chum. Fishing in 90+ depth waters with Spicy Chum can beat the units/minute profits of collecting Gravitino Balls with an upgraded speedy Exocraft, though still a bit below Salvageable Scrap / Ancient Bones.
Additionally, Diurnal & Nocturnal raw fish now have a 1.15x multiplier to their units value, and Storm-only raw fish have a 1.3x multiplier to give a little incentive to seek out these harder to find fish or use their targeted baits.
Adjusted units value for all cooked fish dishes, with smaller, more common fish given larger values relative to their raw ingredients to better compete with using them for bait or releasing them for nanites as they have the most efficient nanite:unit ratio.  Notably now Seafood "Feast" is almost always worthwhile to make (IE all Colossal fish of Uncommon (B) rarity or lower are worth cooking, except for Giant Sunray (B) ). Otherwise usually only Common (C) fish are worth cooking alone, or usually just Small Common fish if combining with other fish / ingredients (with exceptions for the various species-specific recipes for species which don't come in Common and/or Small varieties like turtles, squid, octopus, starfish, eels, etc.)
Cooking 1 Kelp Rice now requires 5x Kelp Sacs (matching how cooking 1 Marrow Flesh takes 5 Marrow Bulbs in PTSd)
Increased the rate that debt is paid off for your settlement ~3x to roughly match the vanilla / expected rate based on settlement daily profits
Small tweaks to Scanning bonus for various Multi-Tools (+ or - 5%/10% bonus): Pistol bonus reduced ~0.88x, Rifle bonus reduced 0.75x, Sentinel bonus increased ~1.1x, Atlantid bonus increased ~1.14x
Unlock cost for Nautilon Geobay at Anomaly reduced ~0.5x
Added to description for Automated Traps to clarify that they will trap fish from various depths regardless of where you place them
Added to description for starship Teleport Receiver to clarify that in PTSd it extends the item interaction range for your starship to 800u.
Added to the descriptions for Autonomous Mining Unit, Oxygen Harvester, Atmosphere Harvester, and Antimatter Reactor to clarify their 10 minute cycle duration time in PTSd and tips for avoiding the vanilla glitch which sometimes clears their inventory

files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-512-0-2-1727391449.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.12
files.changelog_html:
Reduced the quality of Freighter/Frigate upgrade modules looted from destroying civilian freighters or Dreadnoughts from Class B to Class C due to the ease of obtaining them and to incentivize exploring Derelict Freighters more.
Increased the base time between planetary pirate raids by ~1.2x in high-conflict systems and ~1.6x in medium-conflict systems (planetary pirate raids still don't occur in low-conflict systems). In addition, the "Hostile" setting for the "On-Foot Combat" in-game difficulty setting now uses 50% of the base time for planetary pirate raids / sentinel drone spawns instead of 33%
Starship Launcher tech requires ~1.67x as much Uranium to fully recharge, Pulse Engine tech requires 10x as much Pyrite to fully recharge. PTSd changes to starship Launcher & Pulse Engine charging effectiveness now also apply to the special Advanced Launch System & Waveform Engine alternatives
Living Ship shields tech requires 0.5x as much Mordite / Pugneum / Di-hydrogen to fully recharge, launcher tech requires 2x as much Oxygen / Condensed Carbon to fully recharge, pulse engine tech requires 2x Carbon to fully recharge, hyperdrive tech requires ~1.33x Chromatic Metal or Living Slime to fully recharge and can now feasibly be recharged with Processed Meat
Sentinel Interceptor launcher tech requires 0.5x as much Pugneum to fully recharge, pulse engine tech requires 1.25x as much Tritium to recharge, shield tech requires 1.5x Sodium Nitrate to recharge
Warp Hypercore requires 2x the materials to craft
Animus Beam requires 0.5x as much Di-hydrogen to fully recharge
Exocraft Cannon & Nautilon Cannon now consume fuel at 0.5x the vanilla rate
Unlock cost for Tethys Beam and Automated Trap at the Anomaly reduced to ~0.5x, unlock cost for Nautilon Cannon reduced to 0.75x
Increased shield bonus for the Ablative Armour starship tech by ~2.6x so it is no longer weaker than Class C Starshield upgrade modules and perhaps now worth unlocking/installing.
Biological Horror health increased ~1.5x, weakpoint size reduced to ~0.67x, and spit attack damage increased 2x. Number of Horrors spawned at a time decreased to 0.75x, however the number of Horrors which can be actively attacking the player at a time is unchanged.
Rancid Flesh & Purged Ribs value reduced to ~0.75x
Strengthened the reduced Sprinting stamina drain effect from Toxic Storms 5x and the Mining Beam cooling effect from Cold Storms 3x, since these effects are generally much less impactful than the Hot Storm Jetpack efficiency effect or Radiation Storm mining yield effects.
Added clarifications in the mission descriptions & tips for Dreams of the Deep that the High-Power Sonar blueprint needs to be purchased from the Space Anomaly & installed to progress, not the Basic Sonar (due to PTSd splitting the Sonar tech into 2 different techs)
Added to the descriptions for Emeril & Indium Drives to clarify that they also work for red & green star systems. Similarly clarified for AtlasPass v2 & v3 that they also work on low & medium-level security locks.
Added a little more context to the Goods Availability difficulty setting description

files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-512-0-3-1727725082.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.12
files.changelog_html:
The cost to buy Emergency Signal Scanners for Derelict Freighters have the initial price reduced to 0.75x, and the price increases approximately ~0.5x as quickly for each additional one purchased the same day, up to 64k units after the 12th purchase of the day.
Containers / Datapads on Derelict Freighters award ~4x as many nanites. This incentivizes exploring them thoroughly rather than rushing to the end, since more rooms & containers means more nanites. This should make Derelict Freighters one of the very best methods in terms of nanites/minute if also selling/refining other loot into nanites (at the cost of increasingly expensive Emergency Signal Scanners if trying to do them multiple times per day)
Increased nanite reward option at the end of a Derelict Freighter by 3x to make it more competitive with the other choices. Added note to the dialogue choices to display the approximate amount of nanites to be awarded. (Added similar note to nanite reward option dialogue at Manufacturing Facilities)
The Class of Freighter upgrade modules received as a reward option at the end of Derelict Freighters is now truly randomized each run instead of being static based on the star system/region you're in (dialogue window now clarifies that the Tech will be truly random). However they are given generous chances (10% C, 40% B, 30% A, & 20% S Class), and this can be toggled back to vanilla spawn rules with UsePTSdFreiUpgradeClassChances in "PTSd Rewards Remixer.lua"
The amount of Tainted Metal received for trading Crew Manifests / Captain's Logs to Scrap Dealers is now unaffected by the in-game "Natural Resources" difficulty setting. On the "Standard" setting this means you will receive 1.25x more Tainted Metal for trading them in than previously.
As a solution for the vanilla bug where sometimes the mission required to be able to trade in Crew Manifests / Captain's Logs disappears/fails to spawn, you can now activate any Crew Manifest / Captain's Log from your inventory (once outside the Derelict Freighter) to reactivate the "trade in Derelict items at Scrap Dealers or Guild Reps" mission. (Item description now indicates how to do so)
As a backup just in case you're still unable to trade in Derelict Freighter Crew Manifests / Captain's Logs for some other reason (perhaps using the gLonely mod with fewer NPCs available), they can now at least be sold as items for ~0.85x the units you would get for trading them to Guild Reps in PTSd.
The ability to access the secret "discordant interface" terminals at Monoliths in Korvax systems and purchase Atlantid Multi-Tools now unlocks during the "A Leap in the Dark" main story mission after inspecting some Monoliths, instead of after completing the entire main story and starting Autophage missions. This spaces out the unlocking of Atlantid & Staff multi-tools further apart from each other, especially since the large Mining & yield bonuses of Atlantid Multi-Tools are more useful earlier in the game. Added notes to the in-game dialogue and mission tip during "A Leap in the Dark" when Atlantid multi-tools become available.
Amount of Atlantideum required to charge & activate Discordant Interfaces at Korvax Monoliths increased ~2x
Health of Pirate Dreadnoughts hull & all exterior parts reduced to ~0.85x. Pirate Frigate health reduced an additional 0.5x on top of this.
Tweaks to chances & amounts of loot in freighters/cargo pods in regular/outlaw systems. Mainly reducing both the amounts & chances for illegal trade goods in outlaw systems to ~0.8x
Starship Launcher tech requires 1.2x as much Uranium to fully recharge
Reduced the duration of Trade Surges from 3 hours to 1 hour 20 minutes
Adjusted the minimum & maximum possible number of bonuses that can appear on certain upgrade modules that didn't fit the general pattern of other upgrade modules. Mostly lowered the max possible number of bonuses that can appear on some "Rusted" fishing Class upgrades, and made the A & S Class Scanner upgrades always have at least 3 & 4 bonuses.
Since A & S Class Scanner upgrade modules now consistently have at least 3 & 4 bonuses on them, increased the nanite value/price for Scanner upgrades 1.2x again as it was in the past. (X-Class Scanner upgrade price is unchanged since there still is a good chance to get less than 3 or 4 bonuses on those)
Caught a few Monolith rewards I had missed which were still awarding techs from an old tech pool, so they now can teach a wider variety of techs (but not as many weapon techs) and will give random related upgrade modules if you know all the tech in the pool.
Fixed the recipe for refining Flesh Rope + Microprocessors into Salvaged Data not working. Also adjusted the time required for the various PTSd recipes for refining certain items into nanites to scale with the amount of nanites yielded (most of the recipes are now faster)
Added notes to descriptions for the time & weather based baits that diurnal/nocturnal/storm-only fish are more valuable than normal fish.

files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-512-0-4-1728012967.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.12
files.changelog_html:
Adjustments to the bonus stats for most Multi-Tools, mostly to Mining & Damage bonuses (As usual, currently owned multi-tools will need to have their class upgraded to update to the new stats, or use a Save Editor to increase their stat bonuses by the amounts listed below):
• Pistol Mining bonus reduced 0.645x
• Experimental Mining bonus increased 1.33x, Scanning bonus increased 1.04x
• Royal Damage bonus increased ~1.17x, Mining bonus increased ~1.17x
• Alien Damage bonus increased ~1.09x
• Sentinel Mining bonus decreased 0.835x
• Hijacked Laser damage increased 1.55x (to compensate for apparently some recent vanilla change seems to have reduced the effective DPS vs. Sentinels), substance yield decreased 0.65x
• Atlantid Damage bonus decreased 0.8x
• Runic Lens substance yield increased ~1.11x
• Staff Damage bonus increased ~1.29x, Mining bonus increased 1.11x
• All versions of the Mining Beam (Hijacked Laser, Runic Lens, etc.) have their fuel consumption rate increased 1.2x to compensate for how supercharging them reduced their fuel consumption
• Multi-Tool chart on the Mod Description page now changed to display the relevant stats with the Mining Beam (or alternative) supercharged, since it's assumed you'd always be using a supercharged Mining Beam (or alternative) when doing significant mining
Now both Rifles & Pistols act as "starting" weapons which eventually become "obsolete" compared to other multi-tools, as several other tools will have better Resources/sec than Pistols now.
Hijacked Laser Resources/sec rate only drops to ~0.83x of its supercharged rate when not supercharged, unlike the Mining Beam or Runic Lens which drop to ~0.58x of their supercharged rate when not supercharged. So even if leaving the Hijacked Laser un-supercharged, you can potentially get Resources/sec as good or better than other multi-tools (except for Atlantids) even if they use a supercharged mining beam.
• Also, when mining minerals & di-hydrogen the yield from opening Geodes or Crystal Fragments is unchanged, so the Hijacked Laser is especially effective when mining objects with a chance to drop set items like those. Objects which always drop a set amount of items, such as Glowing Minerals, Subterranean Organic Structures, Salvageable Scrap, etc. are even better, essentially having no downside to using Sentinel multi-tool on them, which destroys such objects more than ~7x faster than a Royal multi-tool.
Refining Faecium + Oxygen to make mor Faecium now requires 2x Oxygen
Removed the optional "PTSd Missions and Rewards - No Farther Target Sweep 512.0.3.pak" file from being in the main download zip file by accident last version

files.changelog_html:
This is still an "alpha" version, and so several existing/new features are not yet implemented, and proper bugtesting has not been done. Check the stickied Post for more details
Purple systems can now also be revealed & accessed earlier by taking a new item (Dissonant Compass) unlocked from Hyperion at the Space Anomaly to a Discordant Interface (which become available partway through the Artemis questline in PTSd), then purchasing the Atlantid Drive plans from Hyperion for 12,000 nanites. Revealing purple systems and learning the plans for the Atlantid Drive can instead still be done for free the vanilla way by fully completing the Artemis, Atlas, and Autophage questlines (although the Atlas questline takes much longer to complete in PTSd than vanilla).
Most new techs & products given harder crafting recipes in order to fit into PTSd's progression, requiring Atlas Seeds, new substances, etc.
Various existing products & techs which required the 6th Atlas Seed to craft now require substances found in Purple Systems such as Quartzite, Lithium, etc.
Heart of the Sun now requires Quartzite instead of Gold to craft
Exo-Skiff now requires a Nutrient Processor instead of Cadmium to craft, since it now has a built-in nutrient processor
Vile Queens no longer drop Hypnotic Eye since they now drop Vile Cortex with similar value
Unit value & refining recipes for new substances adjusted to PTSd standards

files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-558-0-3-1741988467.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.58
files.changelog_html:
Gas Giants now have constant hazard effects of all kinds: high heat during the day or in storms, then freezing cold at night due to the different unmixed gases swirling around. There are also constant, low level toxins & radiation due to the types of gases in the air & the exotic materials being crushed. Unlike other planets, even being underground or in caves will still have a slight cold drain from trapped gases.
• In practice, this means that while you still may want to use a rechargeable hazard protection upgrade module for Heat & Cold for storms on gas giants or on extreme gas giants, it's also useful to have decent %-based hazard protection for Toxin & Radiation (since those hazards are weak enough that your base hazard protection will last a decent amount of time)
Adjusted the maximum strength of certain effects from the Nutrient Ingestor to be roughly in the ballpark of the strength of a single powerful upgrade module, as in vanilla some are extremely weak or overly strong.
• E.G. The max mining yield bonus effect and hazard protection effects reduced from +50% to +33%, the max sprint recovery effect increased from +6% to +60%, the max jetpack tank size effect reduced from +300% to +210%, etc.
Nutrient Ingestor only requires Cadmium instead of Emeril, and unlock price is reduced a further 0.5x
Base duration for holding breath underwater reduced to 0.67x (still a net 1.33x increase from pre-World Part II PTSd)
Aeration Membrane strength reduced ~0.9x
Procedural Underwater Hazard upgrade duration reduced to ~0.8x (still roughly 10% longer duration than pre-World Part II PTSd)
Since planets now have ~4-6 fewer plants to scan (hazardous plants & oxygen/sodium/deuterium plants are no longer scannable), the unit & nanite reward for scanning plants is now increased 1.33x. Also animals now reward ~1.5x more nanites for scanning.
The strength of procedural Exocraft Engine & Humboldt Drive upgrade modules follows a smoother progression from the lower to the higher classes
The max speed bonus from Humboldt Drive upgrade modules remains as strong as before Worlds Part II (~1.33x stronger than vanilla currently)
Increased chances of Lightning & Tornadoes on Gas Giants, some small tweaks to other new weather events such as slightly longer durations, etc.
Hopefully fixed issue of meteor strikes not occurring in PTSd
Refining Deuterium from Di-Hydrogen + Silicate Powder now requires 5x Silicate Powder
Changes to types/amounts of enemy starships in space are still missing (Enemy starships will still have PTSd stats, but spawn according to vanilla amounts & types)

files.name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition
files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-558-0-6-1742707507.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.58
files.changelog_html:
Fixed Iteration Ares still saying "Gold Nuggets" in their dialogue when actually offering to trade for Sea Glass
Starting a new Abandoned Mode save will begin with the recipes for all Atlas Seeds already known, since they otherwise may not be possible to obtain (Can use a Save Editor to teach the recipes for an existing Abandoned Mode save). The mod "gPlayer Unlock Purple Access﻿" can also be used in Abandoned Mode to grant access to purple systems
Due to how it was often cheaper to buy a smaller starship & then purchase inventory slots for it compared to buying a larger starship, and how purchasing the components to build an S Class starship would often be much cheaper than buying one of similar size, the pricing for buying both starships & starship inventory slots have been reworked from the ground up:
• Most types of starships should now generally follow the same basic pricing curve and use the same Class-based price multipliers, and so should always have the following relationships: Explorers & Solar ships cost 1x the "normal" price, Fighters cost ~1.15x more, Exotics cost ~1.2x more, and Haulers cost ~0.67x less on a per-slot basis at all Classes (Freighters cost ~3-4x more). Living Ship & Sentinel Interceptor values are unchanged as you cannot purchase them directly with units.
• Shuttles are a special exception, where at C Class and low inventory size they cost ~0.5x as much, but gradually lose their discount at higher Class & inventory size, to where the largest S Class Shuttle costs ~0.85x as much as "normal".
• Prices for specific starships may have gone up or down depending on the type, Class, & inventory size, but in general most of the smallest possible sized starships have increased in price by roughly ~1.5x while prices at larger sizes are very roughly similar.
• The "Small" size class for Shuttles, Fighters, Haulers, Explorers, and Solar ships has the max possible inventory size reduced by ~3-5 slots ("Medium" & "Large" ships of those types are unchanged)
• Solar ships can once again only be found "in the wild" with inventory sizes appropriate for a "Small" sized starship, like in vanilla
• The price to purchase additional inventory slots for starships has been slightly reduced for starship inventories already over ~50 slots (now slowly growing from ~20 million to ~70 million instead of quickly capping at 100 million previously), but has been significantly increased for smaller inventories under 50 slots, and especially under ~25 slots, now starting over ~1 million units at 16 slots.
• The end result is that it should now generally always be more expensive to buy a smaller starship and then purchase inventory slots for it compared to simply buying a larger starship of the same type & Class to begin with. For S Class ships, on average it should cost ~1.33x as much to obtain a larger starship through inventory expansion compared to buying a larger starship, and even more comparatively expensive at lower classes (costing ~4x as much at C Class).
• Additionally, with the cost of buying small starships increased (to break into components for ship-building) and the max size of "Small" starships reduced (most built starships are usually in the "Small" size category), the expected discount for building an S Class starship compared to buying one should be significantly less. And since the built starship will usually be "Small" in most cases, the money saved by building it will usually eventually be outweighed by the increased cost to purchase inventory slots to bring it up to the size of a "Medium" or "Large" starship.
Reduced nanite cost for starship Reactor Cores to ~0.5-0.2x, to better compete with the practical alternative of purchasing & salvaging a small starship of the matching Class.
The unique expedition reward "Pillar of Titan" staff multi-tool is now received at Class C with fewer inventory slots by default, like other unique expedition rewards
Made planets ~70% as likely to contain predators which hunt the player, and made the largest kind of player predators spawn in smaller groups / less frequently. Also slightly reduced vision range of both ground & water predators.
Most buildable objects for bases once again require a nearby base computer to be built first like in vanilla, instead of being freely buildable anywhere on planets. The BuildMostItemsWithoutBase toggle in "gBase Items BasicX.lua" can revert this back to previous behaviour.
Added note to description of Pulse Engine, Pulsing Heart, Launcher, and Neural Assembly upgrade modules explaining that the actual Boost Speed bonus is greater than the UI displays. Also adds note that Neural Assembly upgrade modules in PTSd improve Boost Speed
Correction to earlier patch notes: You actually can use the Quick Menu to recharge all kinds of rechargeable hazard protection upgrade modules on Gas Giants, it's just that the game only lets you select the type of hazard protection which is currently lowest. However, it will still be more economical to rely on periodically recharging you base Hazard Protection instead of the special Toxic or Radiation protection modules on Gas Giants since you'll only need to recharge a single tech instead of two, and they drain much slower than Hot/Cold hazard protection there.

files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-558-0-7-1742878822.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.58
files.changelog_html:
Fixed Golden Vector & Starborn Phoenix starships not always being awarded at C Class with a small inventory by default like other unique expedition reward starships
Unique expedition reward starships now each have their own cost of 4~8 million units to redeem instead of ~1,400 nanites, with the price roughly matching the cost of buying a "regular" version of the same type of starship at that size & Class C. There may still be the vanilla issue where redeeming an expedition ship will be free on the same save slot that you recently completed that expedition and/or already received the expedition version of the ship. (Note that with the recent changes to starship & slot pricing, like any other small starships the expedition reward starships will require investing a significant amount of units to increase their inventory size compared to buying a larger "wild" starship)
The description when redeeming unique expedition starships now notes that you can delete all the pre-installed upgrades if you want to use the starship without affecting game balance/progression (with a special note for the Wraith living ship being on the honor system not to sequence-break visiting Red/Green/Blue stars before obtaining the relevant hyperdrives). Redeeming unique expedition multi-tools gives a similar note, as well as suggesting to trade in a non-Pistol, non-Rifle multi-tool to claim it (as redeeming tools does not have a cost like redeeming ships does).
The % chances for finding S Class starships in Poor/Average/Wealthy/Outlaw systems has been changed from 0%/2%/3%/5% to 1%/1.5%/2.25%/3.4% for a more even distribution. Chances for finding C/B/A Class starships have also been adjusted slightly to progress a little smoother between the different systems levels. (Changes are at the top of "PTSd Ship+MultiTool Rebalance.lua")

files.name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition
files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-561-0-1-1743233212.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.61
files.changelog_html:
Adjusted bonuses from foods in the Nutrient Ingestor again as after further testing in practice they do not actually behave as the UI indicates. The bonuses are actually multiplicative instead of additive despite what the UI shows (which means some of the "bonuses" actually reduced the relevant stat), but also seem to be applied to each tech/upgrade module individually. So for inherently multiplicative stats such as Mining Speed/Yield or Hot/Cold/Rad/Tox Hazard Protection etc. the final bonus becomes exponentially stronger the more tech/upgrade modules with the relevant stat are installed.
• The absolute effect of the Ingestor bonuses always increases the more relevant tech/upgrades you install, unlike most standard upgrade modules. For additive stats this will be a significant %-based improvement no matter how many techs/upgrades are installed, but for multiplicative stats this can range from being small improvements when starting out to very large buffs once you have many relevant techs/upgrades installed.
• Overall it can now be thought of as a "super upgrade module" that should generally give bonuses significantly larger than a single maxed X Class upgrade (assuming you're using high quality food and you've already installed many upgrades) which you can also flexibly change to match the current situation.
• Adjusted description for nutrient ingestor to note how bonuses are actually multiplicative and can increase exponentially with # of installed upgrades for certain bonuses
Gas Giants now spawn a larger variety of vacant buildings such as Plaques, Monoliths, Ruins, etc., and have a higher density of crashed starships/freighters and Damaged Machinery than regular planets (due to vessels getting pulled in by the strong gravity) to make them more rewarding to explore.
Vigilant Stone value increased ~1.6x, but they are no longer received from disturbing Vigilant Eyes directly, instead Mech/Floating Golems have a chance to drop them on defeat. Vigilant Eyes now award some Polished Stone instead.
Increased health, damage, knockback, and other combat stats of new golem / animated stone enemies. Also increased damage from the explosions of small "spider" corrupted quadruped sentinels
Fossil value increased by 1.5x on average and now varies slightly by category, in order of most to least valuable: Skull, Ribcage, Limbs, Tail. While this won't affect the average value of a dig site, it's enough to make the Limbs & Tails worth cooking, while Skulls & Ribcages lose value when cooked.
• Packaged Exhibits are currently a bit more valuable than I'd like as I haven't yet found a way to alter their value, so currently their description heavily discourages selling them.
Since the average value of Ancient Bones sites are now much more consistent without Common/Uncommon/Rare varieties of bones (only really varying based on number of bones at each site), Salvageable Scrap has been adjusted to take over its role as the POI with highly variable profits.
Salvageable Scrap sites now have a chance to drop additional procedural Scrap items from each of the Protective Casings surrounding the Scrap core, so each site should on average have around ~2 Scrap items. While the value of Common & Uncommon Scrap items has been reduced, the value of Rare Scrap items has been increased. This means that compared to Ancient Bones sites, Scrap sites will on average give more profit per minute, but only if you visit enough Scrap sites to start getting some of the Rare Scrap items. However, taking the time to defeat Ancient Golems at Ancient Bones sites for Vigilant Stones can potentially increase their profits/minute depending on how quickly you can defeat them.
The new small boxes in Abandoned Stations now always use their own lootpool instead of sometimes having the same loot as the Abandoned Mode version of Crashed Freighter Containers.
Reduced the chances of finding very valuable items in the new loot boxes on Abandoned Stations such as upgrade modules, Emergency Signal Scanners, inventory expansion items, etc. In exchange, these boxes can now contain a wider variety of generally useful items such as Repair Kits, Larval Cores, Navigation Data, etc.
In Abandoned Mode, Buried Caches & Crashed Freighter Containers are both less likely to contain inventory expansion items, and Crashed Freighter Containers are now more likely to contain the more valuable items such as Emergency Signal Scanners, higher Class upgrade modules, inventory expansion items, etc. compared to Buried Caches.
Re-ordered which Atlas Seeds require which substances to craft, so that anytime a new color of star system becomes accessible, crafting the next Atlas Seed requires stellar metal from that color star (except for purple stars). This should allow fewer techs/items to be crafted "out of sequence" in Abandoned Mode where all Atlas Seed recipes are unlocked from the start in PTSd.
Living Ships can still install standard Teleport Receivers in PTSd, but the new Grasping Tendrils tech now gives them an even longer teleport range than standard starships
Removed alternative recipe for Bone Broth using 2x Softened Marrow, as in PTSd this always loses value

files.file_name: PTSd Missions and Rewards - No Farther Target Swee-2225-561-0-1-1743233239.zip
files.description: This is the PTSd Missions and Rewards module, but re-paked without the PTSd Farther Target Sweep file. Use in place of the default module to keep vanilla distances for most Target Sweep missions to ensure mission markers are shown in multiplayer
files.changelog_html:
Adjusted bonuses from foods in the Nutrient Ingestor again as after further testing in practice they do not actually behave as the UI indicates. The bonuses are actually multiplicative instead of additive despite what the UI shows (which means some of the "bonuses" actually reduced the relevant stat), but also seem to be applied to each tech/upgrade module individually. So for inherently multiplicative stats such as Mining Speed/Yield or Hot/Cold/Rad/Tox Hazard Protection etc. the final bonus becomes exponentially stronger the more tech/upgrade modules with the relevant stat are installed.
• The absolute effect of the Ingestor bonuses always increases the more relevant tech/upgrades you install, unlike most standard upgrade modules. For additive stats this will be a significant %-based improvement no matter how many techs/upgrades are installed, but for multiplicative stats this can range from being small improvements when starting out to very large buffs once you have many relevant techs/upgrades installed.
• Overall it can now be thought of as a "super upgrade module" that should generally give bonuses significantly larger than a single maxed X Class upgrade (assuming you're using high quality food and you've already installed many upgrades) which you can also flexibly change to match the current situation.
• Adjusted description for nutrient ingestor to note how bonuses are actually multiplicative and can increase exponentially with # of installed upgrades for certain bonuses
Gas Giants now spawn a larger variety of vacant buildings such as Plaques, Monoliths, Ruins, etc., and have a higher density of crashed starships/freighters and Damaged Machinery than regular planets (due to vessels getting pulled in by the strong gravity) to make them more rewarding to explore.
Vigilant Stone value increased ~1.6x, but they are no longer received from disturbing Vigilant Eyes directly, instead Mech/Floating Golems have a chance to drop them on defeat. Vigilant Eyes now award some Polished Stone instead.
Increased health, damage, knockback, and other combat stats of new golem / animated stone enemies. Also increased damage from the explosions of small "spider" corrupted quadruped sentinels
Fossil value increased by 1.5x on average and now varies slightly by category, in order of most to least valuable: Skull, Ribcage, Limbs, Tail. While this won't affect the average value of a dig site, it's enough to make the Limbs & Tails worth cooking, while Skulls & Ribcages lose value when cooked.
• Packaged Exhibits are currently a bit more valuable than I'd like as I haven't yet found a way to alter their value, so currently their description heavily discourages selling them.
Since the average value of Ancient Bones sites are now much more consistent without Common/Uncommon/Rare varieties of bones (only really varying based on number of bones at each site), Salvageable Scrap has been adjusted to take over its role as the POI with highly variable profits.
Salvageable Scrap sites now have a chance to drop additional procedural Scrap items from each of the Protective Casings surrounding the Scrap core, so each site should on average have around ~2 Scrap items. While the value of Common & Uncommon Scrap items has been reduced, the value of Rare Scrap items has been increased. This means that compared to Ancient Bones sites, Scrap sites will on average give more profit per minute, but only if you visit enough Scrap sites to start getting some of the Rare Scrap items. However, taking the time to defeat Ancient Golems at Ancient Bones sites for Vigilant Stones can potentially increase their profits/minute depending on how quickly you can defeat them.
The new small boxes in Abandoned Stations now always use their own lootpool instead of sometimes having the same loot as the Abandoned Mode version of Crashed Freighter Containers.
Reduced the chances of finding very valuable items in the new loot boxes on Abandoned Stations such as upgrade modules, Emergency Signal Scanners, inventory expansion items, etc. In exchange, these boxes can now contain a wider variety of generally useful items such as Repair Kits, Larval Cores, Navigation Data, etc.
In Abandoned Mode, Buried Caches & Crashed Freighter Containers are both less likely to contain inventory expansion items, and Crashed Freighter Containers are now more likely to contain the more valuable items such as Emergency Signal Scanners, higher Class upgrade modules, inventory expansion items, etc. compared to Buried Caches.
Re-ordered which Atlas Seeds require which substances to craft, so that anytime a new color of star system becomes accessible, crafting the next Atlas Seed requires stellar metal from that color star (except for purple stars). This should allow fewer techs/items to be crafted "out of sequence" in Abandoned Mode where all Atlas Seed recipes are unlocked from the start in PTSd.

files.file_name: No Man's - Prepare To Sky Edition-2225-561-0-2-1743452376.zip
files.description:
Various balance/progression/difficulty adjustments to the game, with a few new features & bug fixes.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.61
files.changelog_html:
Disturbing Vigilant Eyes is less likely to spawn the floating Living Stones compared to the Golem Mechs, always spawns at least 2 when it spawns the Living Stones, and can now sometimes spawn the Golem & Living Stones together. This also indirectly slightly increases the yield of Vigilant Stones, as Golems are now even more likely to drop 1 or more Vigilant Stones compared to the floating Living Stones.
Memory Stones now each require 64 Polished Stone to access, so that the amount of nanites per minute you can earn from them will increase as your mining & travel speed increases over the game (interaction description now lets the player know they can yield nanites).
Ruins now yield ~0.3x as much Polished Stone as before, as they weren't previously receiving the same adjustments PTSd makes to other minable objects, and in vanilla they yield double what other similar rocks yield.
The reusable fossil exhibit stations for assembling other fossils now require 50 Polished Stone instead of 25 Pure Ferrite to build. (Guide entry on assembling fossils now mentions this)
All other types of decorative exhibits & fossils had a hidden cost of 25 Pure Ferrite to build in vanilla (even when placing individual bones with no mount), which was not refunded when removing / deleting the exhibit/fossil. Those hidden costs have been removed.
Since the new Living Ship Tech Grasping Tendrils stacks additively with Teleport Receiver, they now have the same distance bonus (so installing both will double the teleport distance), tech description updated to make this clear
Bonus Mining Yield during Radiation Storms further reduced from 1.9x to 1.75x
Reduced Chlorine yield of Organic Rocks to ~0.75x
Improved formatting of new description for fossil exhibits
Fixed a formatting error with the description of the PTSd-added Dissonant Compass
Newly recommended mod: Natural Nights (no merging required). Makes nighttime noticeably darker, to the point that it adds a bit of challenge to navigation and makes your torch / exocraft headlights more useful.

.lua files included in download.
Compatible with NMS v5.62
files.changelog_html:
Decreased cost to use Memory Stones from 64 to 32 Polished Stone
Decreased health of Living Stones and "mech" Golems to 0.8x
Increased the cost to purchase inventory slots for Multi-Tools in the 7-15 slot range by roughly ~1.5x on average
Reduced slots on starting Multi-Tool from 8 to 6, and added an initial damaged slot with a special description that explains that the starting Multi-Tool is weak and can never have Damage/Mining/Scanning stat bonuses like all other multi-tools can. (This is also true in vanilla)
The "Mud Hut' and "Ragged Tent" base building objects can once again be built on planets outside of player bases by default (as they could in earlier versions of PTSd alongside most decorative base building objects). Since they are a faster & more convenient method of sheltering from hazards than tunneling underground or creating a roof with the Terrain Editor, in exchange they now have more complex crafting recipes requiring multiple easy to get items such as Marrow Bulbs or Star Silk. This means relying on them requires dedicating some inventory slots to holding their ingredients as a tradeoff. Can be toggled off at the top of gBase Items BasicX.lua
